groups: Flow Taxonomy, Data Providers & Personalization Methods

cards.front: Name the four main personalization methods and when to use each.
cards.back: Merge fields (single value, simple 1:1) · Dynamic content / variations (swap whole components per audience) · Repeater (series of items from a data source) · Saved expressions (filter+sort to return ONE value).
cards.frontHtml: Name the four main personalization methods and when to use each.
cards.backHtml: Merge fields (single value, simple 1:1) · Dynamic content / variations (swap whole components per audience) · Repeater (series of items from a data source) · Saved expressions (filter+sort to return ONE value).

cards.front: What is the difference between Handlebars and AMPscript?
cards.back: Handlebars is the templating language with scripting + conditional logic (code view, data lookups). AMPscript is legacy scripting using the Lookup() function for reading marketing objects.
cards.frontHtml: What is the difference between Handlebars and AMPscript?
cards.backHtml: Handlebars is the templating language with scripting + conditional logic (code view, data lookups). AMPscript is legacy scripting using the Lookup() function for reading marketing objects.

cards.front: What are the key personalization limits?
cards.back: 25 personalization points per item · 15 variations per component · linking components shares one personalization point · subject line + preheader = one component.
cards.frontHtml: What are the key personalization limits?
cards.backHtml: 25 personalization points per item · 15 variations per component · linking components shares one personalization point · subject line + preheader = one component.

cards.front: ⚠️ Can content with variations be exported/imported?
cards.back: No — content with variations cannot be exported or imported.
cards.frontHtml: ⚠️ Can content with variations be exported/imported?
cards.backHtml: No — content with variations cannot be exported or imported.

cards.front: What are the identifiers for marketing object, field, and data graph?
cards.back: Marketing object = mo · field = c · data graph = $dataGraph.Field . ---
cards.frontHtml: What are the identifiers for marketing object, field, and data graph?
cards.backHtml: Marketing object = __mo · field = __c · data graph = $dataGraph.Field.

cards.front: Name the five flow types and their triggers.
cards.back: Audience/Segment (schedule/immediate) · Automation event-triggered (customer action) · Activation-triggered (Data 360 activation publishes) · Broadcast (API/Apex) · On-demand (API/Apex, high-priority).
cards.frontHtml: Name the five flow types and their triggers.
cards.backHtml: Audience/Segment (schedule/immediate) · Automation event-triggered (customer action) · Activation-triggered (Data 360 activation publishes) · Broadcast (API/Apex) · On-demand (API/Apex, high-priority).

cards.front: What are the four audience sources for an audience flow?
cards.back: Segment, List, Record, Campaign . The segment must be published first; recurring runs up to every hour.
cards.frontHtml: What are the four audience sources for an audience flow?
cards.backHtml: Segment, List, Record, Campaign. The segment must be published first; recurring runs up to every hour.

cards.front: What triggers an automation event-triggered flow and how fast does it run?
cards.back: A customer action (click, form submit, record update); runs within 15 minutes . ⚠️ The Create Consent element is available here only.
cards.frontHtml: What triggers an automation event-triggered flow and how fast does it run?
cards.backHtml: A customer action (click, form submit, record update); runs within ~15 minutes. ⚠️ The Create Consent element is available here only.

cards.front: What triggers an activation-triggered flow and what is its refresh cadence?
cards.back: A Data 360 activation publishing. Refresh: 10 min (incremental) / 24 hr (standard). It is the only Data 360 target type and uses MuleSoft or HTTP callout.
cards.frontHtml: What triggers an activation-triggered flow and what is its refresh cadence?
cards.backHtml: A Data 360 activation publishing. Refresh: 10 min (incremental) / 24 hr (standard). It is the only Data 360 target type and uses MuleSoft or HTTP callout.

cards.front: What is unique about a broadcast flow?
cards.back: It uses dynamic segments (membership determined after start) and can run asynchronously.
cards.frontHtml: What is unique about a broadcast flow?
cards.backHtml: It uses dynamic segments (membership determined after start) and can run asynchronously.

cards.front: What is an on-demand flow used for?
cards.back: High-priority API/Apex-triggered sends (e.g., order confirmations); it can include event info like order ID and amount.
cards.frontHtml: What is an on-demand flow used for?
cards.backHtml: High-priority API/Apex-triggered sends (e.g., order confirmations); it can include event info like order ID and amount.

cards.front: What is the campaign ↔ flow cardinality?
cards.back: 1 campaign = many flows ; 1 flow = 1 campaign .
cards.frontHtml: What is the campaign ↔ flow cardinality?
cards.backHtml: 1 campaign = many flows; 1 flow = 1 campaign.

cards.front: How does flow sharing work for campaign-related vs standalone flows?
cards.back: Flows related to a campaign inherit its sharing ; standalone flows are private by default (share via categories + sharing rules, or manually).
cards.frontHtml: How does flow sharing work for campaign-related vs standalone flows?
cards.backHtml: Flows related to a campaign inherit its sharing; standalone flows are private by default (share via categories + sharing rules, or manually).

cards.front: What are the limits for connecting MCE journeys to a campaign?
cards.back: Max 20 journeys per campaign; one campaign per journey. Journey modes: Draft / Running / Finishing / Paused / Stopped.
cards.frontHtml: What are the limits for connecting MCE journeys to a campaign?
cards.backHtml: Max 20 journeys per campaign; one campaign per journey. Journey modes: Draft / Running / Finishing / Paused / Stopped.

cards.front: Name the flow statuses.
cards.back: Preparing · Activated · Finishing · Completed · Scheduled · Canceled · Draft · Error. Only one version active ; ⚠️ a paused flow counts as active .
cards.frontHtml: Name the flow statuses.
cards.backHtml: Preparing · Activated · Finishing · Completed · Scheduled · Canceled · Draft · Error. Only one version active; ⚠️ a paused flow counts as active.

cards.front: Which tiers get On-Canvas Insights vs Flow Reports?
cards.back: On-Canvas Insights = Advanced only ; Flow Reports = Growth + Advanced . ---
cards.frontHtml: Which tiers get On-Canvas Insights vs Flow Reports?
cards.backHtml: On-Canvas Insights = Advanced only; Flow Reports = Growth + Advanced.

cards.front: What data source feeds each of these: segment entry, email merge fields, decision splits, Get Records?
cards.back: Segment entry = DMO layer (Data 360) · email merge fields & decision splits = data graph · Get Records = Salesforce Core (bypasses Data 360).
cards.frontHtml: What data source feeds each of these: segment entry, email merge fields, decision splits, Get Records?
cards.backHtml: Segment entry = DMO layer (Data 360) · email merge fields & decision splits = data graph · Get Records = Salesforce Core (bypasses Data 360).

cards.front: Name the data sources available for messaging content.
cards.back: Data Graph (default) · Unified Individual DMO (fallback) · Event (1 per item) · Offer (max 5) · Personalization Recommender · Content Variable · Salesforce Record · Lookup Data Graph (max 5) · Apex Class (1 per message) · Activation (1 per message) · Marketing Object & Prospect (landing pages/forms only).
cards.frontHtml: Name the data sources available for messaging content.
cards.backHtml: Data Graph (default) · Unified Individual DMO (fallback) · Event (1 per item) · Offer (max 5) · Personalization Recommender · Content Variable · Salesforce Record · Lookup Data Graph (max 5) · Apex Class (1 per message) · Activation (1 per message) · Marketing Object & Prospect (landing pages/forms only).

cards.front: What is a data graph and what does the Default badge mean?
cards.back: A Data 360 object from a primary DMO (usually Unified Individual) plus related objects. The Default badge marks the default graph. Standard vs. real-time (real-time = faster, costs more).
cards.frontHtml: What is a data graph and what does the Default badge mean?
cards.backHtml: A Data 360 object from a primary DMO (usually Unified Individual) plus related objects. The Default badge marks the default graph. Standard vs. real-time (real-time = faster, costs more).

cards.front: ⚠️ When is a data graph locked (cannot be removed/replaced)?
cards.back: If an email has dynamic content variations or a recommender; or once a landing page content block is published . Landing pages should use a real-time graph.
cards.frontHtml: ⚠️ When is a data graph locked (cannot be removed/replaced)?
cards.backHtml: If an email has dynamic content variations or a recommender; or once a landing page content block is published. Landing pages should use a real-time graph.

cards.front: Which data graph do SMS and WhatsApp use?
cards.back: Only the default data graph (not shown in the panel, but works in merge fields).
cards.frontHtml: Which data graph do SMS and WhatsApp use?
cards.backHtml: Only the default data graph (not shown in the panel, but works in merge fields).

cards.front: When is the Unified Individual DMO used as a data source?
cards.back: As a fallback when no data graph exists; it is the only option in Starter/Pro Suite emails.
cards.frontHtml: When is the Unified Individual DMO used as a data source?
cards.backHtml: As a fallback when no data graph exists; it is the only option in Starter/Pro Suite emails.

cards.front: What are the rules for the Event data source?
cards.back: 1 per item ; repeaters do not support custom event data; cannot be removed/replaced after publish.
cards.frontHtml: What are the rules for the Event data source?
cards.backHtml: 1 per item; repeaters do not support custom event data; cannot be removed/replaced after publish.

cards.front: What are the rules for the Personalization Recommender data source?
cards.back: Only trained recommenders on the same data graph; needs ≥1 successful refresh ; can be replaced but not removed ; data works only in a repeater.
cards.frontHtml: What are the rules for the Personalization Recommender data source?
cards.backHtml: Only trained recommenders on the same data graph; needs ≥1 successful refresh; can be replaced but not removed; data works only in a repeater.

cards.front: What are the rules for a lookup data graph?
cards.back: For non-profile data (catalog); needs a primary key; cannot nest ; max 5 .
cards.frontHtml: What are the rules for a lookup data graph?
cards.backHtml: For non-profile data (catalog); needs a primary key; cannot nest; max 5.

cards.front: What data types does a Content Variable support?
cards.back: Boolean, string, date, date time, number, recordId — mapped to Flow data (MuleSoft/HTTP).
cards.frontHtml: What data types does a Content Variable support?
cards.backHtml: Boolean, string, date, date time, number, recordId — mapped to Flow data (MuleSoft/HTTP).

cards.front: ⚠️ What must you do if you change a data source after attributes are used in merge fields?
cards.back: Delete the merge fields, add the new source, and recreate them.
cards.frontHtml: ⚠️ What must you do if you change a data source after attributes are used in merge fields?
cards.backHtml: Delete the merge fields, add the new source, and recreate them.

cards.front: What is required when combining content types (form + landing page)?
cards.back: The data graphs must match . ---
cards.frontHtml: What is required when combining content types (form + landing page)?
cards.backHtml: The data graphs must match.

cards.front: What is a personalization point?
cards.back: A content element eligible for a decision (subject line, preheader, image). The first variation auto-creates the point.
cards.frontHtml: What is a personalization point?
cards.backHtml: A content element eligible for a decision (subject line, preheader, image). The first variation auto-creates the point.

cards.front: What is the difference between a decision and a targeting rule?
cards.back: A decision is who is eligible (each variation ↔ a decision with the same name ). A targeting rule is the conditions for showing a variation (attributes, related attributes, calculated insights, segment memberships).
cards.frontHtml: What is the difference between a decision and a targeting rule?
cards.backHtml: A decision is who is eligible (each variation ↔ a decision with the same name). A targeting rule is the conditions for showing a variation (attributes, related attributes, calculated insights, segment memberships).

cards.front: What is the difference between "All Conditions Are Met" and "Any Conditions Are Met"?
cards.back: All = every condition must be true; Any = at least one condition must be true.
cards.frontHtml: What is the difference between "All Conditions Are Met" and "Any Conditions Are Met"?
cards.backHtml: All = every condition must be true; Any = at least one condition must be true.

cards.front: What is the default variation and can its priority change?
cards.back: It shows when no rule matches; its priority cannot be changed .
cards.frontHtml: What is the default variation and can its priority change?
cards.backHtml: It shows when no rule matches; its priority cannot be changed.

cards.front: What is the difference between cloning and linking a personalization point?
cards.back: Clone = separate copy (component must have no variations; only points on the same data graph are shown). Link = share one point (point must already exist in the content item; component must have no variations).
cards.frontHtml: What is the difference between cloning and linking a personalization point?
cards.backHtml: Clone = separate copy (component must have no variations; only points on the same data graph are shown). Link = share one point (point must already exist in the content item; component must have no variations).

cards.front: What changes propagate across linked components, and what stays independent?
cards.back: Adding/deleting a variation or editing rules/priorities applies to all linked components; content/style edits stay independent .
cards.frontHtml: What changes propagate across linked components, and what stays independent?
cards.backHtml: Adding/deleting a variation or editing rules/priorities applies to all linked components; content/style edits stay independent.

cards.front: What does unlinking a personalization point do?
cards.back: It clones the point ("Copy of …") so the component keeps its settings but becomes independent.
cards.frontHtml: What does unlinking a personalization point do?
cards.backHtml: It clones the point ("Copy of …") so the component keeps its settings but becomes independent.

cards.front: What happens to a repeater when there is no data, and when the layout changes?
cards.back: It is empty if there is no data for the recipient; changing the layout removes content/data/style .
cards.frontHtml: What happens to a repeater when there is no data, and when the layout changes?
cards.backHtml: It is empty if there is no data for the recipient; changing the layout removes content/data/style.

cards.front: How does an objective-based recommender work?
cards.back: It picks the best image per contact at send time (no rules); the canvas shows a placeholder — use Preview with a segment to see real output. ---
cards.frontHtml: How does an objective-based recommender work?
cards.backHtml: It picks the best image per contact at send time (no rules); the canvas shows a placeholder — use Preview with a segment to see real output.

cards.front: What do the Entry, Decision, Action, and Wait elements do?
cards.back: Entry = who enters and when · Decision = branching (first match wins) · Action = send email/SMS, create/update records, create consent, add/remove actionable list · Wait = fixed duration or wait-until-event.
cards.frontHtml: What do the Entry, Decision, Action, and Wait elements do?
cards.backHtml: Entry = who enters and when · Decision = branching (first match wins) · Action = send email/SMS, create/update records, create consent, add/remove actionable list · Wait = fixed duration or wait-until-event.

cards.front: What are the two Decision logic methods?
cards.back: Define Manually (outcomes evaluated in order) vs. Define with AI (Advanced; simultaneous — order has no impact). ⚠️ Define with AI is not supported for Marketing Cloud flows .
cards.frontHtml: What are the two Decision logic methods?
cards.backHtml: Define Manually (outcomes evaluated in order) vs. Define with AI (Advanced; simultaneous — order has no impact). ⚠️ Define with AI is not supported for Marketing Cloud flows.

cards.front: What are the three parts of a decision condition?
cards.back: Resource (data-graph attribute) + Operator (Equals/Greater Than…) + Value .
cards.frontHtml: What are the three parts of a decision condition?
cards.backHtml: Resource (data-graph attribute) + Operator (Equals/Greater Than…) + Value.

cards.front: ⚠️ What flow type do Wait elements require?
cards.back: Autolaunched flows — they cannot be mixed with screens or choice.
cards.frontHtml: ⚠️ What flow type do Wait elements require?
cards.backHtml: Autolaunched flows — they cannot be mixed with screens or choice.

cards.front: What time is used for Wait Until Date with no time specified?
cards.back: 12 AM org time zone .
cards.frontHtml: What time is used for Wait Until Date with no time specified?
cards.backHtml: 12 AM org time zone.

cards.front: ⚠️ Where must a Wait Until Event element sit, and what links are unsupported?
cards.back: It must be immediately after the monitored element; dynamic/merge-field links are unsupported (use Any Link ).
cards.frontHtml: ⚠️ Where must a Wait Until Event element sit, and what links are unsupported?
cards.backHtml: It must be immediately after the monitored element; dynamic/merge-field links are unsupported (use Any Link).

cards.front: What is a Path Experiment and when does it declare a winner?
cards.back: A random split + optimizer (Advanced + Personalization); auto-declares a winner at 95% confidence (Bayesian). Max 10 variations; percentages are targets, not exact counts .
cards.frontHtml: What is a Path Experiment and when does it declare a winner?
cards.backHtml: A random split + optimizer (Advanced + Personalization); auto-declares a winner at 95% confidence (Bayesian). Max 10 variations; percentages are targets, not exact counts.

cards.front: Does manually selecting a Path Experiment winner require a new version?
cards.back: No.
cards.frontHtml: Does manually selecting a Path Experiment winner require a new version?
cards.backHtml: No.

cards.front: What are marketing completion actions and which flow type are they for?
cards.back: Assign to Queue/User and Notify User — Audience flows only .
cards.frontHtml: What are marketing completion actions and which flow type are they for?
cards.backHtml: Assign to Queue/User and Notify User — Audience flows only.

cards.front: What does the Einstein Decision element do?
cards.back: Routes by engagement level (Engagement Frequency / Scoring).
cards.frontHtml: What does the Einstein Decision element do?
cards.backHtml: Routes by engagement level (Engagement Frequency / Scoring).

cards.front: What does the Determine CRM Record for Individual element do?
cards.back: Branches on contact / lead / prospect.
cards.frontHtml: What does the Determine CRM Record for Individual element do?
cards.backHtml: Branches on contact / lead / prospect.

cards.front: What are the restrictions for Send to Journey?
cards.back: Supports only Running journeys with an API event entry source ; Individual ID maps to SubscriberKey.
cards.frontHtml: What are the restrictions for Send to Journey?
cards.backHtml: Supports only Running journeys with an API event entry source; Individual ID maps to SubscriberKey.

cards.front: What are the rules for a Subflow element?
cards.back: Launches another active flow; ⚠️ cannot call flows with wait elements ; variable API names ≤ 40 chars ; calls the active version (API 61.0+).
cards.frontHtml: What are the rules for a Subflow element?
cards.backHtml: Launches another active flow; ⚠️ cannot call flows with wait elements; variable API names ≤ 40 chars; calls the active version (API 61.0+).

cards.front: What are the rules for the Get Records element?
cards.back: Pulls data in; limit 2–20,000 ; needs DLO→DMO mapping for Data Cloud objects.
cards.frontHtml: What are the rules for the Get Records element?
cards.backHtml: Pulls data in; limit 2–20,000; needs DLO→DMO mapping for Data Cloud objects.

cards.front: ⚠️ What happens with an Update Records element that has no filter?
cards.back: It updates ALL records.
cards.frontHtml: ⚠️ What happens with an Update Records element that has no filter?
cards.backHtml: It updates ALL records.

cards.front: Where do deleted records go and how long are they retained?
cards.back: To the Recycle Bin for 15 days .
cards.frontHtml: Where do deleted records go and how long are they retained?
cards.backHtml: To the Recycle Bin for 15 days.

cards.front: When do record changes actually take effect in a flow?
cards.back: Only when the transaction completes .
cards.frontHtml: When do record changes actually take effect in a flow?
cards.backHtml: Only when the transaction completes.

cards.front: What do the Assignment, Loop, Collection Filter, Collection Sort, and Transform elements do?
cards.back: Assignment (consecutive in order) · Loop (Current Item from Loop) · Collection Filter (output null until run; source unchanged) · Collection Sort (up to 3 fields ; modifies directly) · Transform (≤ 1 nested collection ; formula ≤ 255 chars ; no data graphs for joins).
cards.frontHtml: What do the Assignment, Loop, Collection Filter, Collection Sort, and Transform elements do?
cards.backHtml: Assignment (consecutive in order) · Loop (Current Item from Loop) · Collection Filter (output null until run; source unchanged) · Collection Sort (up to 3 fields; modifies directly) · Transform (≤1 nested collection; formula ≤255 chars; no data graphs for joins).

cards.front: ⚠️ Where are In/Not In operators available, and which conditions are NOT filter conditions?
cards.back: In/Not In only in Create/Get/Update Records; Contains/Is Changed are not filter conditions. Multi-select picklist matching is fragile → use INCLUDES .
cards.frontHtml: ⚠️ Where are In/Not In operators available, and which conditions are NOT filter conditions?
cards.backHtml: In/Not In only in Create/Get/Update Records; Contains/Is Changed are not filter conditions. Multi-select picklist matching is fragile → use INCLUDES.

cards.front: What are the rules for flow exit rules?
cards.back: Up to 10 ; evaluated on start/resume; numeric attributes support aggregation (Average/Sum/Max/Min).
cards.frontHtml: What are the rules for flow exit rules?
cards.backHtml: Up to 10; evaluated on start/resume; numeric attributes support aggregation (Average/Sum/Max/Min).

cards.front: What are the rules for engagement signals?
cards.back: Only Engagement-category DMOs ; one related DMO (1:1 or many-to-one); item identifier required for recommenders; identifiers = User/Timestamp/Item/Event; count-based metric by default; custom events from signals = Advanced only .
cards.frontHtml: What are the rules for engagement signals?
cards.backHtml: Only Engagement-category DMOs; one related DMO (1:1 or many-to-one); item identifier required for recommenders; identifiers = User/Timestamp/Item/Event; count-based metric by default; custom events from signals = Advanced only.

cards.front: What is the difference between the flow data graph and the org default data graph?
cards.back: Org default → message personalization; flow graph → decisioning. ---
cards.frontHtml: What is the difference between the flow data graph and the org default data graph?
cards.backHtml: Org default → message personalization; flow graph → decisioning.

cards.front: What is contact point selection?
cards.back: Choosing which fields (email, phone, MAID, etc.) go to the activation target.
cards.frontHtml: What is contact point selection?
cards.backHtml: Choosing which fields (email, phone, MAID, etc.) go to the activation target.

cards.front: What is source priority order and its values?
cards.back: Which value wins when a contact has multiple sources. Values: Primary (Primary Flag mapped) · Personal (For Personal Use = 1) · Business (For Business Use = 1) · Any (no flag).
cards.frontHtml: What is source priority order and its values?
cards.backHtml: Which value wins when a contact has multiple sources. Values: Primary (Primary Flag mapped) · Personal (For Personal Use = 1) · Business (For Business Use = 1) · Any (no flag).

cards.front: ⚠️ What governs contact points — reconciliation rules or source priority?
cards.back: Source priority — reconciliation rules do not govern contact points.
cards.frontHtml: ⚠️ What governs contact points — reconciliation rules or source priority?
cards.backHtml: Source priority — reconciliation rules do not govern contact points.

cards.front: What happens when you remove "Any Source/Any Type"?
cards.back: A smaller population is targeted. ---
cards.frontHtml: What happens when you remove "Any Source/Any Type"?
cards.backHtml: A smaller population is targeted.

cards.front: What are the three ways to create/edit an email?
cards.back: Content tab (Add → Content → Email), the campaign record, or a flow's Send Email Message element.
cards.frontHtml: What are the three ways to create/edit an email?
cards.backHtml: Content tab (Add → Content → Email), the campaign record, or a flow's Send Email Message element.

cards.front: What permissions are needed to create/edit vs publish an email?
cards.back: Create/edit = Marketing Cloud Manager + any CMS contributor role; publish/unpublish = plus content admin/manager.
cards.frontHtml: What permissions are needed to create/edit vs publish an email?
cards.backHtml: Create/edit = Marketing Cloud Manager + any CMS contributor role; publish/unpublish = plus content admin/manager.

cards.front: ⚠️ What personalization is lost when copying an email?
cards.back: Only default variations are copied — other variations, rules, and recommenders are not (merge fields and repeaters are).
cards.frontHtml: ⚠️ What personalization is lost when copying an email?
cards.backHtml: Only default variations are copied — other variations, rules, and recommenders are not (merge fields and repeaters are).

cards.front: What does Convert to Code do and is it reversible?
cards.back: It is one-way and removes dynamic content (repeaters, conditional logic, content variants); you lose drag-and-drop and the Style tab.
cards.frontHtml: What does Convert to Code do and is it reversible?
cards.backHtml: It is one-way and removes dynamic content (repeaters, conditional logic, content variants); you lose drag-and-drop and the Style tab.

cards.front: How long does the View as Web Page link work and what does it reflect?
cards.back: Works 90 days after send; reflects the published version; personalized values re-render against the recipient's current profile on each open.
cards.frontHtml: How long does the View as Web Page link work and what does it reflect?
cards.backHtml: Works 90 days after send; reflects the published version; personalized values re-render against the recipient's current profile on each open.

cards.front: ⚠️ What happens if you manually edit the plain text version?
cards.back: It desyncs from the HTML version — future changes are not included.
cards.frontHtml: ⚠️ What happens if you manually edit the plain text version?
cards.backHtml: It desyncs from the HTML version — future changes are not included.

cards.front: What are the rules for test sends?
cards.back: Up to 5 recipients; they count toward message credits ; the From name must be from an authenticated domain .
cards.frontHtml: What are the rules for test sends?
cards.backHtml: Up to 5 recipients; they count toward message credits; the From name must be from an authenticated domain.

cards.front: What are the file attachment limits?
cards.back: A PDF from CMS, up to 5 MB .
cards.frontHtml: What are the file attachment limits?
cards.backHtml: A PDF from CMS, up to 5 MB.

cards.front: What does CAN-SPAM require in an email?
cards.back: A Physical Address merge field + an opt-out link (Unsubscribe / Preference Manager / custom preference page). ⚠️ Preference Manager and Unsubscribe links do not work in preview.
cards.frontHtml: What does CAN-SPAM require in an email?
cards.backHtml: A Physical Address merge field + an opt-out link (Unsubscribe / Preference Manager / custom preference page). ⚠️ Preference Manager and Unsubscribe links do not work in preview.

cards.front: How does template locking work?
cards.back: Templates are locked by default; nested components mirror the parent (locking cascades). Unlock template-wide (Settings), subject/preheader (lock icons), data sources, or per-component.
cards.frontHtml: How does template locking work?
cards.backHtml: Templates are locked by default; nested components mirror the parent (locking cascades). Unlock template-wide (Settings), subject/preheader (lock icons), data sources, or per-component.

cards.front: What are the rules for dynamic From and Reply addresses?
cards.back: Static From + dynamic display name = subdomain senders (avoids DMARC alignment failures). Dynamic From = root-domain authenticators. Dynamic reply requires an authorized email domain (unauthorized → fallback). Direct reply bypasses RMM . Always configure an authenticated fallback .
cards.frontHtml: What are the rules for dynamic From and Reply addresses?
cards.backHtml: Static From + dynamic display name = subdomain senders (avoids DMARC alignment failures). Dynamic From = root-domain authenticators. Dynamic reply requires an authorized email domain (unauthorized → fallback). Direct reply bypasses RMM. Always configure an authenticated fallback.

cards.front: What are the Distributed Marketing template limits?
cards.back: 30 approved images + 30 approved phrases ; only one default image ; only phrases can be required (locked) — images cannot.
cards.frontHtml: What are the Distributed Marketing template limits?
cards.backHtml: 30 approved images + 30 approved phrases; only one default image; only phrases can be required (locked) — images cannot.

cards.front: What permissions do non-marketer senders need?
cards.back: Send Distributed Marketing Messages + Marketing Cloud Manager .
cards.frontHtml: What permissions do non-marketer senders need?
cards.backHtml: Send Distributed Marketing Messages + Marketing Cloud Manager.

cards.front: How is Distributed Marketing availability configured?
cards.back: An event-triggered flow with the Distributed Marketing and Alerts Message event; Get Records (List Email) + Decision (Status = Scheduled) prevent canceled sends.
cards.frontHtml: How is Distributed Marketing availability configured?
cards.backHtml: An event-triggered flow with the Distributed Marketing and Alerts Message event; Get Records (List Email) + Decision (Status = Scheduled) prevent canceled sends.

cards.front: What does unscheduling do?
cards.back: It cancels the email (and any others scheduled with it in the campaign).
cards.frontHtml: What does unscheduling do?
cards.backHtml: It cancels the email (and any others scheduled with it in the campaign).

cards.front: What are the two Distributed Marketing dashboards?
cards.back: Distributed Sends (Individual Email / Bulk Email / Bulk Email Recipient Activity; your own sends only) + Unified Engagement History (record pages).
cards.frontHtml: What are the two Distributed Marketing dashboards?
cards.backHtml: Distributed Sends (Individual Email / Bulk Email / Bulk Email Recipient Activity; your own sends only) + Unified Engagement History (record pages).

cards.front: What is conversational email and what does it integrate with?
cards.back: Two-way email integrating with Agentforce, Digital Engagement, Data 360 ; replies are analysed for intent → trigger flows, route to agents/human reps, update data in real time. ---
cards.frontHtml: What is conversational email and what does it integrate with?
cards.backHtml: Two-way email integrating with Agentforce, Digital Engagement, Data 360; replies are analysed for intent → trigger flows, route to agents/human reps, update data in real time.

cards.front: Where are landing pages hosted?
cards.back: On the Marketing Landing Pages site (component/template pages) or a marketing site (code-view pages).
cards.frontHtml: Where are landing pages hosted?
cards.backHtml: On the Marketing Landing Pages site (component/template pages) or a marketing site (code-view pages).

cards.front: What is a URL alias and when can it be edited?
cards.back: A vanity URL, editable in Draft only; publishing activates aliases. Statuses: Draft / Active / Inactive (reactivatable).
cards.frontHtml: What is a URL alias and when can it be edited?
cards.backHtml: A vanity URL, editable in Draft only; publishing activates aliases. Statuses: Draft / Active / Inactive (reactivatable).

cards.front: What are the redirect URL rules?
cards.back: Must start with https:// and be < 2,000 characters ; set it up before unpublishing to avoid the "URL no longer exists" page.
cards.frontHtml: What are the redirect URL rules?
cards.backHtml: Must start with https:// and be < 2,000 characters; set it up before unpublishing to avoid the "URL no longer exists" page.

cards.front: When is a form visible?
cards.back: Only once added to a landing page that is published with an active URL alias .
cards.frontHtml: When is a form visible?
cards.backHtml: Only once added to a landing page that is published with an active URL alias.

cards.front: What happens when you publish a landing page with a form?
cards.back: It publishes the form and activates the related flow .
cards.frontHtml: What happens when you publish a landing page with a form?
cards.backHtml: It publishes the form and activates the related flow.

cards.front: What are the SEO rules for landing pages?
cards.back: Public page title, description, head tags; only JSON-LD structured data allowed (no JavaScript); allowed tags = <link , <meta , <script .
cards.frontHtml: What are the SEO rules for landing pages?
cards.backHtml: Public page title, description, head tags; only JSON-LD structured data allowed (no JavaScript); allowed tags = <link>, <meta>, <script>.

cards.front: What are the preview requirements and limitations?
cards.back: Requires site contributor access; merge fields are unresolved ; external images need a Trusted URL list entry.
cards.frontHtml: What are the preview requirements and limitations?
cards.backHtml: Requires site contributor access; merge fields are unresolved; external images need a Trusted URL list entry.

cards.front: ⚠️ What does template locking protect, and what can authors still edit?
cards.back: It protects content/settings only — authors can still edit targeting rules/variations ; clone the personalization point for logic control.
cards.frontHtml: ⚠️ What does template locking protect, and what can authors still edit?
cards.backHtml: It protects content/settings only — authors can still edit targeting rules/variations; clone the personalization point for logic control.

cards.front: What are the two tracking options for landing pages?
cards.back: A consent banner (Marketing Cloud Admin config; Manager + content role to publish) or Relaxed CSP + Head Markup set-consent event (no banner). Custom domain → path /lp . Re-publish the site after banner changes. ---
cards.frontHtml: What are the two tracking options for landing pages?
cards.backHtml: A consent banner (Marketing Cloud Admin config; Manager + content role to publish) or Relaxed CSP + Head Markup set-consent event (no banner). Custom domain → path /lp. Re-publish the site after banner changes.

cards.front: What is the form cardinality rule?
cards.back: One form per landing page; one flow per form ; view modes must match (block ↔ block, code ↔ code).
cards.frontHtml: What is the form cardinality rule?
cards.backHtml: One form per landing page; one flow per form; view modes must match (block ↔ block, code ↔ code).

cards.front: What is the minimum for a form and what are the unique field names?
cards.back: ≥1 input + 1 button. Unique names: Email , FirstName , LastName (case-insensitive, no extra chars).
cards.frontHtml: What is the minimum for a form and what are the unique field names?
cards.backHtml: ≥1 input + 1 button. Unique names: Email, FirstName, LastName (case-insensitive, no extra chars).

cards.front: What are the rules for the write data provider?
cards.back: Account/Contact/Lead/Prospect or a marketing object (default if available, else Lead ); one object at a time; respects FLS .
cards.frontHtml: What are the rules for the write data provider?
cards.backHtml: Account/Contact/Lead/Prospect or a marketing object (default if available, else Lead); one object at a time; respects FLS.

cards.front: What are the read data providers and their limit?
cards.back: Data graph, marketing object, Prospect — for pre-fill + progressive profiling; up to 2 lookup providers (max 1 marketing object + 1 recipient data graph).
cards.frontHtml: What are the read data providers and their limit?
cards.backHtml: Data graph, marketing object, Prospect — for pre-fill + progressive profiling; up to 2 lookup providers (max 1 marketing object + 1 recipient data graph).

cards.front: What field types are supported on forms, and which are not?
cards.back: Supported: Checkbox, Date, Date/Time, Time, Email, Phone, Number, Picklist, Text, Text Area, Text Area (Long), URL. ⚠️ Number of Employees and multi-picklist are unsupported; no duplicate fields; changing a field's API name breaks future saves.
cards.frontHtml: What field types are supported on forms, and which are not?
cards.backHtml: Supported: Checkbox, Date, Date/Time, Time, Email, Phone, Number, Picklist, Text, Text Area, Text Area (Long), URL. ⚠️ Number of Employees and multi-picklist are unsupported; no duplicate fields; changing a field's API name breaks future saves.

cards.front: What are the rules for hidden fields and defaults?
cards.back: Checkbox/Dropdown/Number/Plain Text/Text Area; hidden required fields need a fallback value ; URL parameters (UTM) are supported.
cards.frontHtml: What are the rules for hidden fields and defaults?
cards.backHtml: Checkbox/Dropdown/Number/Plain Text/Text Area; hidden required fields need a fallback value; URL parameters (UTM) are supported.

cards.front: What are the reCAPTCHA v2 rules?
cards.back: Marketing landing pages with forms only; applies to every form once enabled; one per external page ; changing My Domain breaks it.
cards.frontHtml: What are the reCAPTCHA v2 rules?
cards.backHtml: Marketing landing pages with forms only; applies to every form once enabled; one per external page; changing My Domain breaks it.

cards.front: What are the progressive profiling rules?
cards.back: Needs a read data provider; no rules on hidden fields/related objects; changing the read source removes rule connections. ⚠️ Avoid pre-filling PII.
cards.frontHtml: What are the progressive profiling rules?
cards.backHtml: Needs a read data provider; no rules on hidden fields/related objects; changing the read source removes rule connections. ⚠️ Avoid pre-filling PII.

cards.front: What happens when you unpublish a form?
cards.back: It deactivates its flow; Submit stops working; save the flow as a new version to edit/republish. ---
cards.frontHtml: What happens when you unpublish a form?
cards.backHtml: It deactivates its flow; Submit stops working; save the flow as a new version to edit/republish.

cards.front: What makes up the external form embedding code?
cards.back: 2 <script tags + 1 <fragment element ; generated from the published version (republish to refresh).
cards.frontHtml: What makes up the external form embedding code?
cards.backHtml: 2 <script> tags + 1 <fragment> element; generated from the published version (republish to refresh).

cards.front: What security setup is required for external forms?
cards.back: CORS Allowed Origin List + clickjack protection (Trusted Domains for Inline Framing, or allow any page) + Trusted Sites for Scripts → publish the Experience Cloud site (else frame-ancestors 'self' CSP error).
cards.frontHtml: What security setup is required for external forms?
cards.backHtml: CORS Allowed Origin List + clickjack protection (Trusted Domains for Inline Framing, or allow any page) + Trusted Sites for Scripts → publish the Experience Cloud site (else frame-ancestors 'self' CSP error).

cards.front: What is a form handler?
cards.back: A way to capture existing external form submissions into Salesforce (also creates a Data 360 data source).
cards.frontHtml: What is a form handler?
cards.backHtml: A way to capture existing external form submissions into Salesforce (also creates a Data 360 data source).

cards.front: ⚠️ What is the critical rule for external form field names?
cards.back: External field names must exactly match the HTML name attributes. Date = YYYY-MM-DD ; Time = hh:mm:ss ; DateTime = ISO 8601; selected checkbox = true .
cards.frontHtml: ⚠️ What is the critical rule for external form field names?
cards.backHtml: External field names must exactly match the HTML name attributes. Date = YYYY-MM-DD; Time = hh:mm:ss; DateTime = ISO 8601; selected checkbox = true.

cards.front: What is a honeypot field?
cards.back: A spam field that blocks submissions when it has a value; use a generic label, not honeypot .
cards.frontHtml: What is a honeypot field?
cards.backHtml: A spam field that blocks submissions when it has a value; use a generic label, not honeypot.

cards.front: ⚠️ When must you map all fields in a form handler?
cards.back: Before creating the flow — edits afterwards do not reflect automatically.
cards.frontHtml: ⚠️ When must you map all fields in a form handler?
cards.backHtml: Before creating the flow — edits afterwards do not reflect automatically.

cards.front: What is the difference between client-side and server-side form handlers?
cards.back: Client-side (JS snippet): supports web tracking + identity resolution. Server-side (direct POST URL): no tracking/identity resolution; works with strict CSP/third-party builders. Both need a CORS Allowlist entry.
cards.frontHtml: What is the difference between client-side and server-side form handlers?
cards.backHtml: Client-side (JS snippet): supports web tracking + identity resolution. Server-side (direct POST URL): no tracking/identity resolution; works with strict CSP/third-party builders. Both need a CORS Allowlist entry.

cards.front: Where are LinkedIn posts managed?
cards.back: Via the Social Posts related list on the campaigns object; connect a LinkedIn account; Publish Now or Schedule. ---
cards.frontHtml: Where are LinkedIn posts managed?
cards.backHtml: Via the Social Posts related list on the campaigns object; connect a LinkedIn account; Publish Now or Schedule.

cards.front: What is the Campaign Stage field and what is the trap?
cards.back: Derived from all flows: In Planning / In Progress / Completed / Error / Canceled / Paused. ⚠️ One Error flow makes the whole campaign Error.
cards.frontHtml: What is the Campaign Stage field and what is the trap?
cards.backHtml: Derived from all flows: In Planning / In Progress / Completed / Error / Canceled / Paused. ⚠️ One Error flow makes the whole campaign Error.

cards.front: What does the Marketing Calendar show and what is the trap?
cards.back: Campaigns + Campaign Segment Flows + Segment Flows (default); access = Marketing Cloud Admin/Manager or Access Marketing Calendar permission; drag campaigns (not segment flows). ⚠️ Event/form-triggered flows do not appear.
cards.frontHtml: What does the Marketing Calendar show and what is the trap?
cards.backHtml: Campaigns + Campaign Segment Flows + Segment Flows (default); access = Marketing Cloud Admin/Manager or Access Marketing Calendar permission; drag campaigns (not segment flows). ⚠️ Event/form-triggered flows do not appear.

cards.front: What does the NotSentReason field map to, and what are common values?
cards.back: Maps to Engagement Action Reason on the Email Engagement DMO . Common: no consent, no opt-in, unauthorized From, hard bounce, TTL exceeded.
cards.frontHtml: What does the NotSentReason field map to, and what are common values?
cards.backHtml: Maps to Engagement Action Reason on the Email Engagement DMO. Common: no consent, no opt-in, unauthorized From, hard bounce, TTL exceeded.

cards.front: What does on-canvas element analytics show and what are the caveats?
cards.back: Run/success/error counts, avg duration, messaging metrics (Sends, Delivery Rate, Opt-Out Rate, Reads, Failed Deliveries, Response Rate, CTR); needs Tableau Next Included App Business User . ⚠️ Open Details consumes Data Cloud credits ; not available for runs before Winter '25 .
cards.frontHtml: What does on-canvas element analytics show and what are the caveats?
cards.backHtml: Run/success/error counts, avg duration, messaging metrics (Sends, Delivery Rate, Opt-Out Rate, Reads, Failed Deliveries, Response Rate, CTR); needs Tableau Next Included App Business User. ⚠️ Open Details consumes Data Cloud credits; not available for runs before Winter '25.

cards.front: What do AI campaigns do?
cards.back: Draft with Agentforce → brief + campaign preview (name, flow, multichannel content); conversational campaigns add a "Forward to Agent" step; agent actions are powered by Salesforce Flow ; Generate Campaign Insights analyses the first flow . ---
cards.frontHtml: What do AI campaigns do?
cards.backHtml: Draft with Agentforce → brief + campaign preview (name, flow, multichannel content); conversational campaigns add a "Forward to Agent" step; agent actions are powered by Salesforce Flow; Generate Campaign Insights analyses the first flow.

cards.group: Flow Taxonomy, Data Providers & Personalization Methods
cards.front: What is the single orchestration engine for outbound messaging in MC Next?
cards.back: Flow — these are marketing flows (high-scale flows) that run off-core , so governor limits and transaction-scaling concerns don't apply the same way.
cards.frontHtml: What is the single orchestration engine for outbound messaging in MC Next?
cards.backHtml: Flow — these are marketing flows (high-scale flows) that run off-core, so governor limits and transaction-scaling concerns don't apply the same way.

cards.group: Flow Taxonomy, Data Providers & Personalization Methods
cards.front: Name the six flow types and their triggers.
cards.back: Audience (schedule/immediate) · Activation-triggered (activation publishes) · Automation event-triggered (event occurs) · On-demand (REST API, individual) · Broadcast (REST API, dynamic segment) · Data Cloud-triggered (DMO/CIO record changes).
cards.frontHtml: Name the six flow types and their triggers.
cards.backHtml: Audience (schedule/immediate) · Activation-triggered (activation publishes) · Automation event-triggered (event occurs) · On-demand (REST API, individual) · Broadcast (REST API, dynamic segment) · Data Cloud-triggered (DMO/CIO record changes).

cards.group: Flow Taxonomy, Data Providers & Personalization Methods
cards.front: Which two flow types cannot send emails from MC Next?
cards.back: ⚠️ Record-triggered flows (CRM flows) and Data Cloud-triggered flows .
cards.frontHtml: Which two flow types cannot send emails from MC Next?
cards.backHtml: ⚠️ Record-triggered flows (CRM flows) and Data Cloud-triggered flows.

cards.group: Flow Taxonomy, Data Providers & Personalization Methods
cards.front: What re-entry options do audience flows offer?
cards.back: Three, mirroring Journey Builder's contact entry mode: no re-entry , re-entry at any time , re-entry only after exiting .
cards.frontHtml: What re-entry options do audience flows offer?
cards.backHtml: Three, mirroring Journey Builder's contact entry mode: no re-entry, re-entry at any time, re-entry only after exiting.

cards.group: Flow Taxonomy, Data Providers & Personalization Methods
cards.front: Why can an activation be used as the personalization source?
cards.back: Because you can append related-object attributes to the activation — merge fields and repeaters reference enriched activation attributes without additional send-time lookups .
cards.frontHtml: Why can an activation be used as the personalization source?
cards.backHtml: Because you can append related-object attributes to the activation — merge fields and repeaters reference enriched activation attributes without additional send-time lookups.

cards.group: Flow Taxonomy, Data Providers & Personalization Methods
cards.front: What two values are required for an on-demand flow API call?
cards.back: Email address and individual ID . ⚠️ The ID needn't match a Data 360 Individual record — it just can't be null . No Individual DMO record is created, but engagement lands in the Email Engagement DMO .
cards.frontHtml: What two values are required for an on-demand flow API call?
cards.backHtml: Email address and individual ID. ⚠️ The ID needn't match a Data 360 Individual record — it just can't be null. No Individual DMO record is created, but engagement lands in the Email Engagement DMO.

cards.group: Flow Taxonomy, Data Providers & Personalization Methods
cards.front: What is the typical latency of an on-demand flow?
cards.back: 1–3 seconds — ideal for one-time passcodes, order confirmations, password resets, real-time service alerts.
cards.frontHtml: What is the typical latency of an on-demand flow?
cards.backHtml: ~1–3 seconds — ideal for one-time passcodes, order confirmations, password resets, real-time service alerts.

cards.group: Flow Taxonomy, Data Providers & Personalization Methods
cards.front: What segment type must a broadcast flow use?
cards.back: A dynamic segment , evaluated at execution time using variables passed into the flow. Static and parameterized criteria can be combined.
cards.frontHtml: What segment type must a broadcast flow use?
cards.backHtml: A dynamic segment, evaluated at execution time using variables passed into the flow. Static and parameterized criteria can be combined.

cards.group: Flow Taxonomy, Data Providers & Personalization Methods
cards.front: Name the eight data providers.
cards.back: Data graph · Event · Activation · Salesforce record · Apex class · Personalization recommender · Lookup graph · Offer.
cards.frontHtml: Name the eight data providers.
cards.backHtml: Data graph · Event · Activation · Salesforce record · Apex class · Personalization recommender · Lookup graph · Offer.

cards.group: Flow Taxonomy, Data Providers & Personalization Methods
cards.front: Can a message use both an activation and an event data provider?
cards.back: ⚠️ No — each requires a specific flow orchestration pattern, so using both creates a conflict in how data is bound to the message.
cards.frontHtml: Can a message use both an activation and an event data provider?
cards.backHtml: ⚠️ No — each requires a specific flow orchestration pattern, so using both creates a conflict in how data is bound to the message.

cards.group: Flow Taxonomy, Data Providers & Personalization Methods
cards.front: What does an event data provider NOT support?
cards.back: Related collections — it supports direct attributes from the event DMO only (e.g., Sales Order yes, Sales Order Product no).
cards.frontHtml: What does an event data provider NOT support?
cards.backHtml: Related collections — it supports direct attributes from the event DMO only (e.g., Sales Order yes, Sales Order Product no).

cards.group: Flow Taxonomy, Data Providers & Personalization Methods
cards.front: What are content variables, and what types do they support?
cards.back: Custom placeholders defined in the email, populated at runtime from Salesforce Flow (any flow data source incl. MuleSoft/HTTP). Types: boolean, text, date, dateTime, number, recordId . The content defines the placeholders; the flow supplies the values .
cards.frontHtml: What are content variables, and what types do they support?
cards.backHtml: Custom placeholders defined in the email, populated at runtime from Salesforce Flow (any flow data source incl. MuleSoft/HTTP). Types: boolean, text, date, dateTime, number, recordId. The content defines the placeholders; the flow supplies the values.

cards.group: Flow Taxonomy, Data Providers & Personalization Methods
cards.front: What is a marketing object, and what's the MCE comparison?
cards.back: A marketer-managed table of data queried at runtime to personalize content. Closest MCE comparison = a data extension . Supports text, number, decimal ; full refresh replaces records.
cards.frontHtml: What is a marketing object, and what's the MCE comparison?
cards.backHtml: A marketer-managed table of data queried at runtime to personalize content. Closest MCE comparison = a data extension. Supports text, number, decimal; full refresh replaces records.

cards.group: Flow Taxonomy, Data Providers & Personalization Methods
cards.front: How does MC Next personalization differ from MCE?
cards.back: MCE relies primarily on data extensions (sendable/non-sendable). MC Next offers data providers, content variables, and marketing objects . ⚠️ Not every MCE AMPscript function is supported.
cards.frontHtml: How does MC Next personalization differ from MCE?
cards.backHtml: MCE relies primarily on data extensions (sendable/non-sendable). MC Next offers data providers, content variables, and marketing objects. ⚠️ Not every MCE AMPscript function is supported.

cards.group: Flow Taxonomy, Data Providers & Personalization Methods
cards.front: Which personalization methods are marketer-friendly vs developer-oriented?
cards.back: Marketer: merge fields, repeaters, dynamic content. Developer: Handlebars, AMPscript.
cards.frontHtml: Which personalization methods are marketer-friendly vs developer-oriented?
cards.backHtml: Marketer: merge fields, repeaters, dynamic content. Developer: Handlebars, AMPscript.

cards.group: Flow Taxonomy, Data Providers & Personalization Methods

cards.back: A fallback value used when the customer's data is missing (e.g., "Friend" for a missing first name). ---

cards.back: Draft content and create sections.
cards.frontHtml: What can the Content Builder agent do?
cards.backHtml: Draft content and create sections.

cards.front: What does Einstein Segments do and what does it require?
cards.back: Turns natural language into a segment; requires a Unified Individual DMO with ≥10 records .
cards.frontHtml: What does Einstein Segments do and what does it require?
cards.backHtml: Turns natural language into a segment; requires a Unified Individual DMO with ≥10 records.

cards.front: What is Einstein Data Prism?
cards.back: The grounding layer for Einstein segments — it scans metadata, auto-generates descriptions, and uses a vector database. Validate/exclude via Metadata Studio . ⚠️ Not supported in Gov Cloud Plus.
cards.frontHtml: What is Einstein Data Prism?

cards.front: What does Einstein Segments strip out when generating a segment?
cards.back: Demographic attributes and attributes that would return < 10 results . ---
cards.frontHtml: What does Einstein Segments strip out when generating a segment?

cards.front: What is the difference between a channel and an agent in conversational messaging?
cards.back: Channel = pipe (delivery); Agent = brain (LLM + Data 360).
cards.frontHtml: What is the difference between a channel and an agent in conversational messaging?
cards.backHtml: Channel = pipe (delivery); Agent = brain (LLM + Data 360).

cards.front: What four components make up the conversational ecosystem?
cards.back: Channel + Flow + Agent + Data 360 .
cards.frontHtml: What four components make up the conversational ecosystem?
cards.backHtml: Channel + Flow + Agent + Data 360.

cards.front: What is the difference between subagents and actions?
cards.back: Subagents = job description (boundaries); Actions = tools (get info / update records).
cards.frontHtml: What is the difference between subagents and actions?
cards.backHtml: Subagents = job description (boundaries); Actions = tools (get info / update records).

cards.front: What are the four stages of the conversational lifecycle?
cards.back: Trigger → Routing/intent → Execution → Handoff/resolution.
cards.frontHtml: What are the four stages of the conversational lifecycle?
cards.backHtml: Trigger → Routing/intent → Execution → Handoff/resolution.

cards.front: What are the key conversational KPIs?
cards.back: Deflection, engagement, and conversion. ---
cards.frontHtml: What are the key conversational KPIs?
cards.backHtml: Deflection, engagement, and conversion.

cards.front: Which edition is required for each predictive AI feature?
cards.back: Send Time Optimization (STO) = Growth (global model) / Advanced · Metrics Guard = Growth + Advanced · Engagement Scoring = Advanced only · Engagement Frequency = Advanced only.
cards.frontHtml: Which edition is required for each predictive AI feature?
cards.backHtml: Send Time Optimization (STO) = Growth (global model) / Advanced · Metrics Guard = Growth + Advanced · Engagement Scoring = Advanced only · Engagement Frequency = Advanced only.

cards.front: ⚠️ What is counterintuitive about the Metrics Guard score?
cards.back: Lower = more likely real (a lower score means a lower likelihood of being a bot).
cards.frontHtml: ⚠️ What is counterintuitive about the Metrics Guard score?
cards.backHtml: Lower = more likely real (a lower score means a lower likelihood of being a bot).

cards.front: What prerequisite do STO, Engagement Scoring, and Engagement Frequency share?
cards.back: An identity resolution ruleset with Individual as the primary object.
cards.frontHtml: What prerequisite do STO, Engagement Scoring, and Engagement Frequency share?
cards.backHtml: An identity resolution ruleset with Individual as the primary object.

cards.front: What are the three scoring model types and their range?
cards.back: Engagement , Fit , and Overall — scored 0–100 . Account scoring is Advanced only .
cards.frontHtml: What are the three scoring model types and their range?
cards.backHtml: Engagement, Fit, and Overall — scored 0–100. Account scoring is Advanced only.

cards.front: How does scoring frequency affect cost?
cards.back: More frequent scoring = more credits consumed. ---
cards.frontHtml: How does scoring frequency affect cost?
cards.backHtml: More frequent scoring = more credits consumed.

cards.front: Name the components of the Einstein Trust Layer.
cards.back: Toxicity detection · dynamic grounding (anti-hallucination) · PII masking · zero data retention · encryption · audit trail · human escalation.
cards.frontHtml: Name the components of the Einstein Trust Layer.
cards.backHtml: Toxicity detection · dynamic grounding (anti-hallucination) · PII masking · zero data retention · encryption · audit trail · human escalation.

cards.front: What does dynamic grounding do?
cards.back: It grounds AI responses in real data to prevent hallucination.
cards.frontHtml: What does dynamic grounding do?

cards.front: What does zero data retention mean in the Trust Layer?
cards.back: Prompts and responses are not retained by the LLM provider. ---

cards.backHtml: Prompts and responses are not retained by the LLM provider.

cards.back: Segment Creation (NL → editable segment criteria) · Campaign Creation (briefs, flows, multi-channel content) · Content Creation (drafts/refines email, LP, SMS) · Journey Decisioning (picks journey/flow + personalizes) · Account Discovery (account insights + buying group members).

cards.group: The Five Agents & Predictive AI Deep Dive
cards.front: What does the Account Discovery agent do?
cards.back: Provides account insights and identifies potential buying group members — helps discover stakeholders and guide nurturing/follow-up.
