decks.title: Flashcards — Agentic, Conversational, Data Architecture & Email

cards.front: What is the defining difference between traditional automation and agentic marketing?
cards.back: Automation follows a fixed, human-configured path; agentic marketing lets the marketer state a strategy while AI agents create content, build audiences, personalize, optimize, and orchestrate handoffs autonomously.
cards.frontHtml: What is the defining difference between traditional automation and agentic marketing?
cards.backHtml: Automation follows a fixed, human-configured path; agentic marketing lets the marketer state a strategy while AI agents create content, build audiences, personalize, optimize, and orchestrate handoffs autonomously.

cards.front: What three pillars set Marketing Cloud Next apart from retrofitted-AI platforms?
cards.back: (1) Actionable data (one unified dataset), (2) cross-departmental workflows (Sales/Service/Commerce), (3) autonomous Agentforce-native AI agents.
cards.frontHtml: What three pillars set Marketing Cloud Next apart from retrofitted-AI platforms?
cards.backHtml: (1) Actionable data (one unified dataset), (2) cross-departmental workflows (Sales/Service/Commerce), (3) autonomous Agentforce-native AI agents.

cards.front: Name the three waves of Marketing Cloud evolution.
cards.back: Wave 1 Automation → Wave 2 Real-Time → Wave 3 Agentic.
cards.frontHtml: Name the three waves of Marketing Cloud evolution.
cards.backHtml: Wave 1 Automation → Wave 2 Real-Time → Wave 3 Agentic.

cards.front: What does "zero copy data access" mean?
cards.back: Connecting directly to an external data platform (Snowflake, BigQuery) and reading data in place without physically moving/copying it.
cards.frontHtml: What does "zero copy data access" mean?
cards.backHtml: Connecting directly to an external data platform (Snowflake, BigQuery) and reading data in place without physically moving/copying it.

cards.front: What is the "pipe vs. brain" distinction in conversational marketing?
cards.back: The channel (SMS/WhatsApp/email) is the pipe that delivers messages and receives replies; the agent (Agentforce) is the brain that analyzes text with LLMs + Data 360.
cards.frontHtml: What is the "pipe vs. brain" distinction in conversational marketing?
cards.backHtml: The channel (SMS/WhatsApp/email) is the pipe that delivers messages and receives replies; the agent (Agentforce) is the brain that analyzes text with LLMs + Data 360.

cards.front: What are the four components of the conversational ecosystem?
cards.back: Channel (interface), Flow (traffic controller), Agent (intelligence), Data 360 (memory).
cards.frontHtml: What are the four components of the conversational ecosystem?
cards.backHtml: Channel (interface), Flow (traffic controller), Agent (intelligence), Data 360 (memory).

cards.front: What's the difference between a subagent and an action?
cards.back: A subagent defines the boundaries of what the agent may discuss (the "job description"); an action is a tool to actually do things (Get Information or Update Records).
cards.frontHtml: What's the difference between a subagent and an action?
cards.backHtml: A subagent defines the boundaries of what the agent may discuss (the "job description"); an action is a tool to actually do things (Get Information or Update Records).

cards.front: What are the four stages of a conversation's lifecycle?
cards.back: (1) Trigger, (2) Routing & engagement (intent recognition), (3) Execution (retrieve/update via actions), (4) Handoff or resolution.
cards.frontHtml: What are the four stages of a conversation's lifecycle?
cards.backHtml: (1) Trigger, (2) Routing & engagement (intent recognition), (3) Execution (retrieve/update via actions), (4) Handoff or resolution.

cards.front: Name the three core KPIs for conversational marketing.
cards.back: Deflection rate (no human intervention), engagement rate (replies vs. clicks), conversion rate (sale/booking).
cards.frontHtml: Name the three core KPIs for conversational marketing.
cards.backHtml: Deflection rate (no human intervention), engagement rate (replies vs. clicks), conversion rate (sale/booking).

cards.front: Name four mechanisms of the Einstein Trust Layer.
cards.back: Toxicity detection, dynamic grounding (anti-hallucination), PII data masking, zero data retention, encryption, audit trail, human escalation (any four).
cards.frontHtml: Name four mechanisms of the Einstein Trust Layer.
cards.backHtml: Toxicity detection, dynamic grounding (anti-hallucination), PII data masking, zero data retention, encryption, audit trail, human escalation (any four).

cards.front: How does the Trust Layer protect PII sent to an LLM?
cards.back: It detects PII (credit cards, phones, addresses), replaces it with anonymized placeholders before the prompt reaches the LLM, then unmasks the response.
cards.frontHtml: How does the Trust Layer protect PII sent to an LLM?
cards.backHtml: It detects PII (credit cards, phones, addresses), replaces it with anonymized placeholders before the prompt reaches the LLM, then unmasks the response.

cards.front: What are DLO, DMO, and Unified Individual, in order?
cards.back: DLO (raw data lake object, "intake"), DMO (standardized data model object), Unified Individual (identity-resolved single profile).
cards.frontHtml: What are DLO, DMO, and Unified Individual, in order?
cards.backHtml: DLO (raw data lake object, "intake"), DMO (standardized data model object), Unified Individual (identity-resolved single profile).

cards.front: What primary object does Marketing Cloud Next require for a data graph?
cards.back: Unified Individual (the segment driving the flow must also be built on Unified Individual).
cards.frontHtml: What primary object does Marketing Cloud Next require for a data graph?
cards.backHtml: Unified Individual (the segment driving the flow must also be built on Unified Individual).

cards.front: Why doesn't data automatically become available just because it's in Data 360?
cards.back: A field must be explicitly included in the data graph before Marketing Cloud Next can access it for personalization/decisioning.
cards.frontHtml: Why doesn't data automatically become available just because it's in Data 360?
cards.backHtml: A field must be explicitly included in the data graph before Marketing Cloud Next can access it for personalization/decisioning.

cards.front: What three decisions must an admin make before building a data graph?
cards.back: Which objects to include, which fields are needed (can't be removed after save), and refresh frequency.
cards.frontHtml: What three decisions must an admin make before building a data graph?
cards.backHtml: Which objects to include, which fields are needed (can't be removed after save), and refresh frequency.

cards.front: Which flow element draws data from Salesforce Core directly (bypassing Data 360)?
cards.back: The Get Records element (e.g., Contacts, Leads, Accounts).
cards.frontHtml: Which flow element draws data from Salesforce Core directly (bypassing Data 360)?
cards.backHtml: The Get Records element (e.g., Contacts, Leads, Accounts).

cards.front: Name the five stages of the data ingestion workflow.
cards.back: (1) Data stream → DLO, (2) DMO mapping, (3) identity resolution → Unified Individual, (4) segment refresh, (5) data graph refresh.
cards.frontHtml: Name the five stages of the data ingestion workflow.
cards.backHtml: (1) Data stream → DLO, (2) DMO mapping, (3) identity resolution → Unified Individual, (4) segment refresh, (5) data graph refresh.

cards.front: How often does identity resolution run by default, and why is it the least predictable stage?
cards.back: Once per day (more often for smaller change sets); depends on schedule and change volume, so a few hours up to 24 hours.
cards.frontHtml: How often does identity resolution run by default, and why is it the least predictable stage?
cards.backHtml: ~Once per day (more often for smaller change sets); depends on schedule and change volume, so a few hours up to ~24 hours.

cards.front: How do the CRM connector's streaming vs. batch ingestion differ in latency?
cards.back: CDC streaming lands in the DLO in 3 minutes; batch fallback (unsupported CDC or formula fields) checks every 10 minutes.
cards.frontHtml: How do the CRM connector's streaming vs. batch ingestion differ in latency?
cards.backHtml: CDC streaming lands in the DLO in ~3 minutes; batch fallback (unsupported CDC or formula fields) checks ~every 10 minutes.

cards.front: How does a Decision element evaluate outcomes?
cards.back: Outcomes are evaluated in order and the first match wins; unmatched contacts follow the default (catch-all) outcome.
cards.frontHtml: How does a Decision element evaluate outcomes?
cards.backHtml: Outcomes are evaluated in order and the first match wins; unmatched contacts follow the default (catch-all) outcome.

cards.front: What are the three parts of a decision condition?
cards.back: Resource (data-graph attribute), Operator (Equals/Greater Than/etc.), Value (typed entry or field reference).
cards.frontHtml: What are the three parts of a decision condition?
cards.backHtml: Resource (data-graph attribute), Operator (Equals/Greater Than/etc.), Value (typed entry or field reference).

cards.front: How does the flow data graph differ from the org default data graph?
cards.back: The org default populates message personalization; the flow data graph determines what the flow can evaluate for decisioning.
cards.frontHtml: How does the flow data graph differ from the org default data graph?
cards.backHtml: The org default populates message personalization; the flow data graph determines what the flow can evaluate for decisioning.

cards.front: What two capabilities does a Path Experiment combine?
cards.back: Random Split (distribute contacts across paths) and Path Optimizer (evaluate which path performs best).
cards.frontHtml: What two capabilities does a Path Experiment combine?
cards.backHtml: Random Split (distribute contacts across paths) and Path Optimizer (evaluate which path performs best).

cards.front: At what confidence level does automatic Path Experiment selection declare a winner?
cards.back: 95% confidence against all other paths; the delayed group then follows the winning path.
cards.frontHtml: At what confidence level does automatic Path Experiment selection declare a winner?
cards.backHtml: 95% confidence against all other paths; the delayed group then follows the winning path.

cards.front: Which edition includes Path Experiments, and what permission is required?
cards.back: Advanced Edition only; requires Marketing Cloud Manager or Admin permission set + personalization features.
cards.frontHtml: Which edition includes Path Experiments, and what permission is required?
cards.backHtml: Advanced Edition only; requires Marketing Cloud Manager or Admin permission set + personalization features.

cards.front: What is a formula resource used for in a flow?
cards.back: A computed value (e.g., Today()-30 ) that a Decision element can reference, such as testing recency.
cards.frontHtml: What is a formula resource used for in a flow?
cards.backHtml: A computed value (e.g., Today()-30) that a Decision element can reference, such as testing recency.

cards.front: What's the difference between promotional and transactional message purpose?
cards.back: Promotional = marketing content, requires opt-in consent; transactional = related to a customer action (receipt, reset), no subscription needed.
cards.frontHtml: What's the difference between promotional and transactional message purpose?
cards.backHtml: Promotional = marketing content, requires opt-in consent; transactional = related to a customer action (receipt, reset), no subscription needed.

cards.front: What are the three core parts of the email editor?
cards.back: Canvas (structure), components panel (elements), properties sidebar (per-component settings).
cards.frontHtml: What are the three core parts of the email editor?
cards.backHtml: Canvas (structure), components panel (elements), properties sidebar (per-component settings).

cards.front: How often is personalization tracking setup performed?
cards.back: Once per org (Customer Engagement → Personalization Setup).
cards.frontHtml: How often is personalization tracking setup performed?
cards.backHtml: Once per org (Customer Engagement → Personalization Setup).

cards.front: What's the difference between linking and cloning a personalization point?
cards.back: Linking shares one personalization point across components (updates apply everywhere); cloning creates a separate copy with its own rules.
cards.frontHtml: What's the difference between linking and cloning a personalization point?
cards.backHtml: Linking shares one personalization point across components (updates apply everywhere); cloning creates a separate copy with its own rules.

cards.front: What does a saved expression do?
cards.back: Defines which single value to return from data when multiple are possible, using filters/sorting (e.g., most recent purchase); reusable across emails/channels.
cards.frontHtml: What does a saved expression do?
cards.backHtml: Defines which single value to return from data when multiple are possible, using filters/sorting (e.g., most recent purchase); reusable across emails/channels.

cards.front: What three parts make up the consent composite key?
cards.back: Communication Subscription (topic) + Contact Point (email/phone) + Engagement Channel Type (Email/SMS/WhatsApp).
cards.frontHtml: What three parts make up the consent composite key?
cards.backHtml: Communication Subscription (topic) + Contact Point (email/phone) + Engagement Channel Type (Email/SMS/WhatsApp).

cards.front: What does Marketing Cloud Next's strict opt-in rule mean?
cards.back: If no consent record exists for a recipient on a subscription, the system treats them as opted out and blocks the send (absence of "Yes" = "No").
cards.frontHtml: What does Marketing Cloud Next's strict opt-in rule mean?
cards.backHtml: If no consent record exists for a recipient on a subscription, the system treats them as opted out and blocks the send (absence of "Yes" = "No").

cards.front: Does "Unsubscribe from all" persist as a permanent block?
cards.back: No — it removes the contact from all existing subscriptions but doesn't prevent a future opt-in on a newly created subscription.
cards.frontHtml: Does "Unsubscribe from all" persist as a permanent block?
cards.backHtml: No — it removes the contact from all existing subscriptions but doesn't prevent a future opt-in on a newly created subscription.

cards.front: What is SMS opt-out scope?
cards.back: Per sender code — opting out of one code doesn't affect other codes from the same brand (not global per phone number).
cards.frontHtml: What is SMS opt-out scope?
cards.backHtml: Per sender code — opting out of one code doesn't affect other codes from the same brand (not global per phone number).

cards.front: Why must you never delete a Communication Subscription?
cards.back: Deleting it cascades and permanently destroys all related historical consent data (the audit trail). Instead, remove it from Preference Pages.
cards.frontHtml: Why must you never delete a Communication Subscription?
cards.backHtml: Deleting it cascades and permanently destroys all related historical consent data (the audit trail). Instead, remove it from Preference Pages.

cards.front: What flow actions write consent, and which must be avoided?
cards.back: Use Create Consent (Data Cloud Record-Triggered) or Consent Request (Automation Event/On-Demand); avoid MessagingConsent / MessagingConsentV2 .
cards.frontHtml: What flow actions write consent, and which must be avoided?
cards.backHtml: Use Create Consent (Data Cloud Record-Triggered) or Consent Request (Automation Event/On-Demand); avoid MessagingConsent / MessagingConsentV2.

cards.front: What are the five steps of a double opt-in flow?
cards.back: (1) Data capture, (2) transactional confirmation email, (3) click verification link, (4) Consent Request action writes OPT IN, (5) verified subscriber.
cards.frontHtml: What are the five steps of a double opt-in flow?
cards.backHtml: (1) Data capture, (2) transactional confirmation email, (3) click verification link, (4) Consent Request action writes OPT_IN, (5) verified subscriber.

cards.front: What four pieces establish a trusted sending identity?
cards.back: Physical address, authenticated sending domain (DKIM/SPF/DMARC), authenticated from addresses, branded tracking domain.
cards.frontHtml: What four pieces establish a trusted sending identity?
cards.backHtml: Physical address, authenticated sending domain (DKIM/SPF/DMARC), authenticated from addresses, branded tracking domain.

cards.front: What three functions does Reply Mail Management perform?
cards.back: Delete auto-responses, optional auto-response acknowledgment, routing to a monitored inbox (plus opt-out keyword processing).
cards.frontHtml: What three functions does Reply Mail Management perform?
cards.backHtml: Delete auto-responses, optional auto-response acknowledgment, routing to a monitored inbox (plus opt-out keyword processing).

cards.front: What does Einstein Metrics Guard do?
cards.back: Uses AI to filter non-human activity (bot scans, security checks) so open/click rates reflect real engagement.
cards.frontHtml: What does Einstein Metrics Guard do?
cards.backHtml: Uses AI to filter non-human activity (bot scans, security checks) so open/click rates reflect real engagement.

cards.front: What happens when you copy an email that includes personalization?
cards.back: Only the default variations of dynamic content components are copied — other variations and personalization rules aren't. A Personalization recommender isn't copied either (but its merge fields and repeaters are).
cards.frontHtml: What happens when you copy an email that includes personalization?
cards.backHtml: Only the default variations of dynamic content components are copied — other variations and personalization rules aren't. A Personalization recommender isn't copied either (but its merge fields and repeaters are).

cards.front: What does converting an email to code remove, and can you undo it?
cards.back: It removes dynamic content — repeaters, conditional logic, and content variants — and you lose drag-and-drop components and Style tab styling. You can't undo the conversion.
cards.frontHtml: What does converting an email to code remove, and can you undo it?
cards.backHtml: It removes dynamic content — repeaters, conditional logic, and content variants — and you lose drag-and-drop components and Style tab styling. You can't undo the conversion.

cards.front: How long does a View as Web Page link work, and what does it re-render?
cards.back: It becomes active when sent and works for 90 days. It reflects the published version at send time, but personalized values re-render against the recipient's current profile each time the link is opened.
cards.frontHtml: How long does a View as Web Page link work, and what does it re-render?
cards.backHtml: It becomes active when sent and works for 90 days. It reflects the published version at send time, but personalized values re-render against the recipient's current profile each time the link is opened.

cards.front: What happens when you manually edit an email's plain text version?
cards.back: It's no longer in sync with the original — future changes to the original aren't included. Restore discards plain-text edits.
cards.frontHtml: What happens when you manually edit an email's plain text version?
cards.backHtml: It's no longer in sync with the original — future changes to the original aren't included. Restore discards plain-text edits.

cards.front: How many test recipients can you send to, and what do test sends count toward?
cards.back: Up to five comma-separated addresses; test sends count toward message credits. The From name must be from an authenticated domain.
cards.frontHtml: How many test recipients can you send to, and what do test sends count toward?
cards.backHtml: Up to five comma-separated addresses; test sends count toward message credits. The From name must be from an authenticated domain.

cards.front: What file type and size limit apply to email attachments?
cards.back: PDF files from Salesforce CMS, up to 5 MB.
cards.frontHtml: What file type and size limit apply to email attachments?
cards.backHtml: PDF files from Salesforce CMS, up to 5 MB.

cards.front: What are the three opt-out link options for promotional emails?
cards.back: Unsubscribe (immediate unsubscribe from the email's subscription + confirmation page), Preference Manager (manage individual email preferences), or a custom preference page URL.
cards.frontHtml: What are the three opt-out link options for promotional emails?
cards.backHtml: Unsubscribe (immediate unsubscribe from the email's subscription + confirmation page), Preference Manager (manage individual email preferences), or a custom preference page URL.

cards.front: How does locking work for email template content?
cards.back: Template-wide settings and components are locked by default; nested components mirror the parent (locking/unlocking cascades). Unlock via Settings (template-wide), lock icons (subject/preheader), Data Sources tab, or per-component "Allow users to modify this component".
cards.frontHtml: How does locking work for email template content?
cards.backHtml: Template-wide settings and components are locked by default; nested components mirror the parent (locking/unlocking cascades). Unlock via Settings (template-wide), lock icons (subject/preheader), Data Sources tab, or per-component "Allow users to modify this component".

cards.front: When should you use a static vs. dynamic From address?
cards.back: Static From + dynamic display name when sending from an authenticated subdomain (avoids DMARC alignment failures); dynamic From when you authenticate the root domain (personal addresses align with the sending domain).
cards.frontHtml: When should you use a static vs. dynamic From address?
cards.backHtml: Static From + dynamic display name when sending from an authenticated subdomain (avoids DMARC alignment failures); dynamic From when you authenticate the root domain (personal addresses align with the sending domain).

cards.front: What does a dynamic reply address require, and what happens if the domain isn't authorized?
cards.back: It requires an authorized email domain. MC Next validates each resolved reply address's domain; if not authorized, it uses the fallback address.
cards.frontHtml: What does a dynamic reply address require, and what happens if the domain isn't authorized?
cards.backHtml: It requires an authorized email domain. MC Next validates each resolved reply address's domain; if not authorized, it uses the fallback address.

cards.front: How does a dynamic reply address interact with Reply Mail Management?
cards.back: Direct reply bypasses RMM (no auto-reply/out-of-office/unsubscribe processing); RMM routing forwards replies to conversational agents, shared inboxes, or Sales/Service Cloud routing rules.
cards.frontHtml: How does a dynamic reply address interact with Reply Mail Management?
cards.backHtml: Direct reply bypasses RMM (no auto-reply/out-of-office/unsubscribe processing); RMM routing forwards replies to conversational agents, shared inboxes, or Sales/Service Cloud routing rules.

cards.front: What happens when a dynamic From/reply value is missing at send time?
cards.back: MC Next uses the configured fallback — always configure a verified, authenticated address as the fallback to maintain deliverability.
cards.frontHtml: What happens when a dynamic From/reply value is missing at send time?
cards.backHtml: MC Next uses the configured fallback — always configure a verified, authenticated address as the fallback to maintain deliverability.

cards.front: What are the two ways to source a dynamic email address?
cards.back: From an associated user (contact owner, account manager, customer success manager) or from a custom field (brand, publication, or region address).
cards.frontHtml: What are the two ways to source a dynamic email address?
cards.backHtml: From an associated user (contact owner, account manager, customer success manager) or from a custom field (brand, publication, or region address).

decks.title: Flashcards — Business Units, Campaigns, Content & Beyond

cards.front: What enforces data isolation between business units?
cards.back: A one-to-one mapping between a business unit and a data space (each business unit → exactly one data space, not shared).
cards.frontHtml: What enforces data isolation between business units?
cards.backHtml: A one-to-one mapping between a business unit and a data space (each business unit → exactly one data space, not shared).

cards.front: What are the two business unit member roles and their key difference?
cards.back: Marketer-Standard (can activate flows) vs. Marketer-ReadOnly (can't activate; can send messages + view dashboards).
cards.frontHtml: What are the two business unit member roles and their key difference?
cards.backHtml: Marketer-Standard (can activate flows) vs. Marketer-ReadOnly (can't activate; can send messages + view dashboards).

cards.front: How many business units can you create, and can you deactivate the last one?
cards.back: Up to 150; you can't deactivate the last remaining business unit (and deactivation is permanent).
cards.frontHtml: How many business units can you create, and can you deactivate the last one?
cards.backHtml: Up to 150; you can't deactivate the last remaining business unit (and deactivation is permanent).

cards.front: Which Einstein feature is NOT supported with business units?
cards.back: Einstein Metrics Guard.
cards.frontHtml: Which Einstein feature is NOT supported with business units?
cards.backHtml: Einstein Metrics Guard.

cards.front: What's the cardinality between campaigns and flows?
cards.back: One campaign can contain multiple flows; each flow relates to only one campaign.
cards.frontHtml: What's the cardinality between campaigns and flows?
cards.backHtml: One campaign can contain multiple flows; each flow relates to only one campaign.

cards.front: Name three marketing-oriented flow types and their triggers.
cards.back: Audience Flow (schedule/segment), Automation Event-Triggered Flow (event), Activation-Triggered Flow (activation publish), Broadcast/On-Demand (API call).
cards.frontHtml: Name three marketing-oriented flow types and their triggers.
cards.backHtml: Audience Flow (schedule/segment), Automation Event-Triggered Flow (event), Activation-Triggered Flow (activation publish), Broadcast/On-Demand (API call).

cards.front: How does a Decision element evaluate outcomes?
cards.back: Like IF/ELSE — outcomes evaluated in order, first match wins, unmatched records follow the default path.
cards.frontHtml: How does a Decision element evaluate outcomes?
cards.backHtml: Like IF/ELSE — outcomes evaluated in order, first match wins, unmatched records follow the default path.

cards.front: What happens to a Wait element when you pause a flow?
cards.back: Pause duration counts toward total wait time; past-due tasks complete immediately on resume.
cards.frontHtml: What happens to a Wait element when you pause a flow?
cards.backHtml: Pause duration counts toward total wait time; past-due tasks complete immediately on resume.

cards.front: How many exit rules can a flow have, and when are they evaluated?
cards.back: Up to 10; evaluated each time a user starts or resumes a flow.
cards.frontHtml: How many exit rules can a flow have, and when are they evaluated?
cards.backHtml: Up to 10; evaluated each time a user starts or resumes a flow.

cards.front: What three Salesforce Personalization concepts power dynamic content?
cards.back: Personalization point, decision, and targeting rule.
cards.frontHtml: What three Salesforce Personalization concepts power dynamic content?
cards.backHtml: Personalization point, decision, and targeting rule.

cards.front: Max personalization points per content item and variations per component?
cards.back: 25 personalization points per item; 15 variations per component.
cards.frontHtml: Max personalization points per content item and variations per component?
cards.backHtml: 25 personalization points per item; 15 variations per component.

cards.front: What are the GSM-7 vs UCS-2 SMS character limits?
cards.back: GSM-7 = 160 chars; UCS-2 (Unicode/emoji) = 70 chars; segmented messages add a header (153/67).
cards.frontHtml: What are the GSM-7 vs UCS-2 SMS character limits?
cards.backHtml: GSM-7 = 160 chars; UCS-2 (Unicode/emoji) = 70 chars; segmented messages add a header (153/67).

cards.front: Which five SMS opt-out keywords are always reserved?
cards.back: STOP, QUIT, CANCEL, END, UNSUBSCRIBE.
cards.frontHtml: Which five SMS opt-out keywords are always reserved?
cards.backHtml: STOP, QUIT, CANCEL, END, UNSUBSCRIBE.

cards.front: What does "published" mean for an email (vs. sent)?
cards.back: Published = ready to send in a flow; customers see it only when the campaign/flow is activated.
cards.frontHtml: What does "published" mean for an email (vs. sent)?
cards.backHtml: Published = ready to send in a flow; customers see it only when the campaign/flow is activated.

cards.front: Key difference between a prospect and a lead?
cards.back: Prospect is unqualified (marketing-owned, top of funnel); lead is qualified (sales-owned, middle of funnel).
cards.frontHtml: Key difference between a prospect and a lead?
cards.backHtml: Prospect is unqualified (marketing-owned, top of funnel); lead is qualified (sales-owned, middle of funnel).

cards.front: Can you create a Unified Individual record manually?
cards.back: No — created only by syncing + identity resolution harmonization.
cards.frontHtml: Can you create a Unified Individual record manually?
cards.backHtml: No — created only by syncing + identity resolution harmonization.

cards.front: What happens when converting a prospect to an existing lead with empty fields?
cards.back: Only empty fields in the existing lead are overwritten by prospect values.
cards.frontHtml: What happens when converting a prospect to an existing lead with empty fields?
cards.backHtml: Only empty fields in the existing lead are overwritten by prospect values.

cards.front: Name three product-related marketing triggers.
cards.back: Product Back In Stock, Product Low Inventory, Product Price Drop (also Abandoned Cart/Page/Browse).
cards.frontHtml: Name three product-related marketing triggers.
cards.backHtml: Product Back In Stock, Product Low Inventory, Product Price Drop (also Abandoned Cart/Page/Browse).

cards.front: Difference between Inactivity Period and Job Frequency in a trigger?
cards.back: Inactivity = wait after last interaction; Job Frequency = how often the trigger job evaluates customers.
cards.frontHtml: Difference between Inactivity Period and Job Frequency in a trigger?
cards.backHtml: Inactivity = wait after last interaction; Job Frequency = how often the trigger job evaluates customers.

cards.front: What permission set configures marketing triggers?
cards.back: Marketing Triggers Admin.
cards.frontHtml: What permission set configures marketing triggers?
cards.backHtml: Marketing Triggers Admin.

cards.front: What engagement types does Opportunity Influence use for attribution?
cards.back: Email and SMS click activities (not opens, not external sites).
cards.frontHtml: What engagement types does Opportunity Influence use for attribution?
cards.backHtml: Email and SMS click activities (not opens, not external sites).

cards.front: What's the attribution window for Opportunity Influence?
cards.back: 30 days before opportunity creation to the date it's Closed/Won.
cards.frontHtml: What's the attribution window for Opportunity Influence?
cards.backHtml: 30 days before opportunity creation to the date it's Closed/Won.

cards.front: Difference between first-touch and last-touch attribution?
cards.back: First-touch credits the first campaign engaged; last-touch credits the last campaign before close.
cards.frontHtml: Difference between first-touch and last-touch attribution?
cards.backHtml: First-touch credits the first campaign engaged; last-touch credits the last campaign before close.

cards.front: Name the four B2B Analytics dashboards.
cards.back: Account-Based Marketing, Pipeline, Marketing Manager, B2B Attribution.
cards.frontHtml: Name the four B2B Analytics dashboards.
cards.backHtml: Account-Based Marketing, Pipeline, Marketing Manager, B2B Attribution.

cards.front: What's the Campaign ROI% formula?
cards.back: (Revenue − Cost) / Cost.
cards.frontHtml: What's the Campaign ROI% formula?
cards.backHtml: (Revenue − Cost) / Cost.

cards.front: Max approved images/phrases, and which can be "required"?
cards.back: 30 images + 30 phrases; only phrases can be required (locked), one default image.
cards.frontHtml: Max approved images/phrases, and which can be "required"?
cards.backHtml: 30 images + 30 phrases; only phrases can be required (locked), one default image.

cards.front: What two permission sets does a non-marketing sender need?
cards.back: Send Distributed Marketing Messages + Marketing Cloud Manager.
cards.frontHtml: What two permission sets does a non-marketing sender need?
cards.backHtml: Send Distributed Marketing Messages + Marketing Cloud Manager.

cards.front: Difference between Click Rate and Click-Through Rate (CTR)?
cards.back: Click Rate = clicks/sends; CTR = clicks/opens (different denominators).
cards.frontHtml: Difference between Click Rate and Click-Through Rate (CTR)?
cards.backHtml: Click Rate = clicks/sends; CTR = clicks/opens (different denominators).

cards.front: What's the email delivery rate formula?
cards.back: (sends − bounces) / sends.
cards.frontHtml: What's the email delivery rate formula?
cards.backHtml: (sends − bounces) / sends.

cards.front: What's the push open rate denominator?
cards.back: Opened / Delivered (not sent).
cards.frontHtml: What's the push open rate denominator?
cards.backHtml: Opened / Delivered (not sent).

cards.front: What are the three marketing object data types and their limits?
cards.back: Text (up to 255 chars), Number (integer up to 18 digits), Decimal (decimal up to 18 digits). Max length can't be changed after creation.
cards.frontHtml: What are the three marketing object data types and their limits?
cards.backHtml: Text (up to 255 chars), Number (integer up to 18 digits), Decimal (decimal up to 18 digits). Max length can't be changed after creation.

cards.front: What are the Growth vs. Advanced allocations for marketing object storage and count?
cards.back: Growth = 10 GB / 25 objects; Advanced = 40 GB / 100 objects; 100 columns per object (both).
cards.frontHtml: What are the Growth vs. Advanced allocations for marketing object storage and count?
cards.backHtml: Growth = 10 GB / 25 objects; Advanced = 40 GB / 100 objects; 100 columns per object (both).

cards.front: What identifier suffix marks a marketing object vs. a field vs. a data graph field?
cards.back: Object = API name + mo ; field = API name + c ; data graph field = $dataGraph.<Field .
cards.frontHtml: What identifier suffix marks a marketing object vs. a field vs. a data graph field?
cards.backHtml: Object = API name + __mo; field = API name + __c; data graph field = $dataGraph.<Field>.

cards.front: What function/helper reads marketing object data in AMPscript vs. Handlebars?
cards.back: AMPscript uses Lookup() (e.g., %=v(@points)=% ); Handlebars uses queryFirst type="MO" .
cards.frontHtml: What function/helper reads marketing object data in AMPscript vs. Handlebars?
cards.backHtml: AMPscript uses Lookup() (e.g., %=v(@points)=%); Handlebars uses queryFirst type="MO".

cards.front: How does an actionable list differ from a segment?
cards.back: Actionable list = fixed/static collection (leads OR contacts, not both); segment = dynamic, rule-based.
cards.frontHtml: How does an actionable list differ from a segment?
cards.backHtml: Actionable list = fixed/static collection (leads OR contacts, not both); segment = dynamic, rule-based.

cards.front: Who can manually remove members from an actionable list record page?
cards.back: Only the list's creator (flow automation can also remove members).
cards.frontHtml: Who can manually remove members from an actionable list record page?
cards.backHtml: Only the list's creator (flow automation can also remove members).

cards.front: How do you create a marketing object, and what happens to the data types?
cards.back: Import a CSV file (Data Management → Marketing Objects → New → From File). The object contains only the CSV's columns; MC Next infers each column's data type from the file.
cards.frontHtml: How do you create a marketing object, and what happens to the data types?
cards.backHtml: Import a CSV file (Data Management → Marketing Objects → New → From File). The object contains only the CSV's columns; MC Next infers each column's data type from the file.

cards.front: Can a marketing object have multiple primary key fields or composite keys?
cards.back: You can select more than one primary key field, but marketing objects don't support composite keys.
cards.frontHtml: Can a marketing object have multiple primary key fields or composite keys?
cards.backHtml: You can select more than one primary key field, but marketing objects don't support composite keys.

cards.front: What does a Full Refresh do to a marketing object, and what must the CSV match?
cards.back: It deletes the object's data and replaces it with the CSV's data. The file must have the same columns as the marketing object. Needs Manage Marketing Objects + Modify All Marketing Object Records.
cards.frontHtml: What does a Full Refresh do to a marketing object, and what must the CSV match?
cards.backHtml: It deletes the object's data and replaces it with the CSV's data. The file must have the same columns as the marketing object. Needs Manage Marketing Objects + Modify All Marketing Object Records.

cards.front: Which marketing object field properties can't be changed after creation?
cards.back: Field API name, data type, and primary key designation. To change them, delete the field and recreate it — which permanently removes all data in that field.
cards.frontHtml: Which marketing object field properties can't be changed after creation?
cards.backHtml: Field API name, data type, and primary key designation. To change them, delete the field and recreate it — which permanently removes all data in that field.

cards.front: What happens while a marketing object schema change is processing?
cards.back: It typically completes in a few seconds; you can't make additional schema changes during processing (fields show a "Read Only" indicator), but the object remains available for queries and record creation.
cards.frontHtml: What happens while a marketing object schema change is processing?
cards.backHtml: It typically completes in a few seconds; you can't make additional schema changes during processing (fields show a "Read Only" indicator), but the object remains available for queries and record creation.

cards.front: When can't you delete a marketing object, and what happens when you do?
cards.back: You can't delete it if any other object refers to its data (remove references from content, campaigns, briefs, flows first). Deleting removes all contained data permanently — it can't be restored.
cards.frontHtml: When can't you delete a marketing object, and what happens when you do?
cards.backHtml: You can't delete it if any other object refers to its data (remove references from content, campaigns, briefs, flows first). Deleting removes all contained data permanently — it can't be restored.

cards.front: What do ViewAllMarketingObjectRecords vs. ManageMarketingObjects grant?
cards.back: ViewAllMarketingObjectRecords = view records from any marketing object. ManageMarketingObjects = view records + create and delete marketing objects.
cards.frontHtml: What do ViewAllMarketingObjectRecords vs. ManageMarketingObjects grant?
cards.backHtml: ViewAllMarketingObjectRecords = view records from any marketing object. ManageMarketingObjects = view records + create and delete marketing objects.

cards.front: How do you make the Data Management tab appear for marketing users?
cards.back: Setup → Profiles → Marketing User → Edit → Tab Settings → Data Management → Default On. Users can also add/rearrange it in the tab bar.
cards.frontHtml: How do you make the Data Management tab appear for marketing users?
cards.backHtml: Setup → Profiles → Marketing User → Edit → Tab Settings → Data Management → Default On. Users can also add/rearrange it in the tab bar.

cards.front: When should you insert records manually vs. import a CSV?
cards.back: Use Add Records (Data Explorer) for a small number of manual entries; use CSV import for larger data loads.
cards.frontHtml: When should you insert records manually vs. import a CSV?
cards.backHtml: Use Add Records (Data Explorer) for a small number of manual entries; use CSV import for larger data loads.

cards.front: In a workspace share chain (A→B→C), why might an asset fail to publish to C?
cards.back: Sharing is not transitive — publishing to C doesn't publish A's assets; you must share the original source A directly to each target.
cards.frontHtml: In a workspace share chain (A→B→C), why might an asset fail to publish to C?
cards.backHtml: Sharing is not transitive — publishing to C doesn't publish A's assets; you must share the original source A directly to each target.

cards.front: How does engagement differ between a prospect and a lead?
cards.back: A prospect may have interacted only once; a lead is actively engaging with sales or marketing content.
cards.frontHtml: How does engagement differ between a prospect and a lead?
cards.backHtml: A prospect may have interacted only once; a lead is actively engaging with sales or marketing content.

cards.front: What's the conversion potential of a prospect vs. a lead?
cards.back: Prospect = low to medium; lead = medium to high.
cards.frontHtml: What's the conversion potential of a prospect vs. a lead?
cards.backHtml: Prospect = low to medium; lead = medium to high.

cards.front: What's required to create a contact, and what happens when converting to an existing contact?
cards.back: An account is required for creating a contact; when converting a prospect to an existing contact, creating a new account is disabled.
cards.frontHtml: What's required to create a contact, and what happens when converting to an existing contact?
cards.backHtml: An account is required for creating a contact; when converting a prospect to an existing contact, creating a new account is disabled.

cards.front: Can prospects be added to campaigns, and how?
cards.back: Yes — prospects are treated as unified individuals, so you can create a unified individual segment, define rules for prospects, and add them to campaigns.
cards.frontHtml: Can prospects be added to campaigns, and how?
cards.backHtml: Yes — prospects are treated as unified individuals, so you can create a unified individual segment, define rules for prospects, and add them to campaigns.

cards.front: What must the Consent Status column include when importing prospects via CSV?
cards.back: Opt-in values, if you plan to send marketing emails.
cards.frontHtml: What must the Consent Status column include when importing prospects via CSV?
cards.backHtml: Opt-in values, if you plan to send marketing emails.

cards.front: What's the minimum information needed to add a prospect manually?
cards.back: At least last name, email, or phone number.
cards.frontHtml: What's the minimum information needed to add a prospect manually?
cards.backHtml: At least last name, email, or phone number.

cards.front: Which flow type converts prospects to leads on engagement score, and how?
cards.back: A Data 360-Triggered Flow — Start element = engagement score object, condition = engagement score greater than a value → convert to lead.
cards.frontHtml: Which flow type converts prospects to leads on engagement score, and how?
cards.backHtml: A Data 360-Triggered Flow — Start element = engagement score object, condition = engagement score greater than a value → convert to lead.

cards.front: Which flow type converts prospects to contacts, and what's the example condition?
cards.back: A Record-Triggered Flow on Prospect (created or updated) with the Convert Prospect action; e.g., if ProspectStatus equals Qualified → convert to contact. Data 360-triggered and form-triggered flows can also convert.
cards.frontHtml: Which flow type converts prospects to contacts, and what's the example condition?
cards.backHtml: A Record-Triggered Flow on Prospect (created or updated) with the Convert Prospect action; e.g., if ProspectStatus equals Qualified → convert to contact. Data 360-triggered and form-triggered flows can also convert.

cards.front: What inputs does the Convert Prospect flow action require?
cards.back: Prospect ID; Converted Status (valid picklist option + Converted checkbox selected); Existing/New Contact; Existing/New Account; optional Existing/New Opportunity.
cards.frontHtml: What inputs does the Convert Prospect flow action require?
cards.backHtml: Prospect ID; Converted Status (valid picklist option + Converted checkbox selected); Existing/New Contact; Existing/New Account; optional Existing/New Opportunity.

cards.front: How does Multi-Currency affect prospect → lead conversion?
cards.back: If the lead's annual revenue is empty but the prospect's is populated, the prospect's Currency ISO code + annual revenue replace the lead's. Different currency codes → the prospect's currency code wins to avoid conversion problems.
cards.frontHtml: How does Multi-Currency affect prospect → lead conversion?
cards.backHtml: If the lead's annual revenue is empty but the prospect's is populated, the prospect's Currency ISO code + annual revenue replace the lead's. Different currency codes → the prospect's currency code wins to avoid conversion problems.

cards.front: What's the Title length gotcha when converting a prospect?
cards.back: Prospect Title allows up to 128 characters, but conversion fails if the lead's Title field would contain more than 80 characters.
cards.frontHtml: What's the Title length gotcha when converting a prospect?
cards.backHtml: Prospect Title allows up to 128 characters, but conversion fails if the lead's Title field would contain more than 80 characters.

cards.front: How do prospect address fields map to Contact and Account?
cards.back: City → Mailing City / Billing City; Country → Mailing Country / Mailing Country; State/Province → Mailing State/Province / Billing State/Province; Zip → Mailing Zip / Billing Zip.
cards.frontHtml: How do prospect address fields map to Contact and Account?
cards.backHtml: City → Mailing City / Billing City; Country → Mailing Country / Mailing Country; State/Province → Mailing State/Province / Billing State/Province; Zip → Mailing Zip / Billing Zip.

cards.front: How does the prospect Company field map on conversion?
cards.back: Lead: Company; Contact: Account Name; Account: Account Name.
cards.frontHtml: How does the prospect Company field map on conversion?
cards.backHtml: Lead: Company; Contact: Account Name; Account: Account Name.

cards.front: How does Prospect Currency map on conversion?
cards.back: Lead: Lead Currency; Contact: Contact Currency; Account: Account Currency.
cards.frontHtml: How does Prospect Currency map on conversion?
cards.backHtml: Lead: Lead Currency; Contact: Contact Currency; Account: Account Currency.

cards.front: What do Lead Assignment Rules determine, and what does each rule entry specify?
cards.back: They determine the record owner after a prospect converts to a lead. Each rule entry specifies: processing order, the condition the lead must match, and the user assigned.
cards.frontHtml: What do Lead Assignment Rules determine, and what does each rule entry specify?
cards.backHtml: They determine the record owner after a prospect converts to a lead. Each rule entry specifies: processing order, the condition the lead must match, and the user assigned.

cards.front: Which restrictions apply to prospects?
cards.back: Can't add a prospect as a campaign member; not supported in Data Import Wizard; can't clone or bulk delete prospects; converted prospects don't show in list view; status values = lead status values.
cards.frontHtml: Which restrictions apply to prospects?
cards.backHtml: Can't add a prospect as a campaign member; not supported in Data Import Wizard; can't clone or bulk delete prospects; converted prospects don't show in list view; status values = lead status values.

cards.front: What's the difference between default and required content in a Distributed Marketing template?
cards.back: A default appears automatically but the user can edit/remove it (only one default image); a required phrase is locked and can't be edited. If neither, the section shows as a blank placeholder.
cards.frontHtml: What's the difference between default and required content in a Distributed Marketing template?
cards.backHtml: A default appears automatically but the user can edit/remove it (only one default image); a required phrase is locked and can't be edited. If neither, the section shows as a blank placeholder.

cards.front: How do you force non-marketers to choose only approved subject lines/preheaders?
cards.back: Lock the subject line/preheader field — if unlocked, users can enter custom text even when approved options are available.
cards.frontHtml: How do you force non-marketers to choose only approved subject lines/preheaders?
cards.backHtml: Lock the subject line/preheader field — if unlocked, users can enter custom text even when approved options are available.

cards.front: What flow elements make an approved template available and prevent canceled sends?
cards.back: An event-triggered flow with the Distributed Marketing and Alerts Message event; Wait Until Date (scheduled sends), Get Records (List Email), Decision (Status = Scheduled), and Send Email Message on the scheduled branch. Canceled emails go down the alternate path and aren't sent.
cards.frontHtml: What flow elements make an approved template available and prevent canceled sends?
cards.backHtml: An event-triggered flow with the Distributed Marketing and Alerts Message event; Wait Until Date (scheduled sends), Get Records (List Email), Decision (Status = Scheduled), and Send Email Message on the scheduled branch. Canceled emails go down the alternate path and aren't sent.

cards.front: What happens when you unschedule a Distributed Marketing email?
cards.back: It cancels the email so it isn't sent — and if it was scheduled with other emails in a campaign, those are canceled too. To send on a new schedule, recreate it.
cards.frontHtml: What happens when you unschedule a Distributed Marketing email?

decks.title: Flashcards — Campaigns, Flows & Flow Elements Deep Dive

cards.front: What's the relationship between campaigns and flows?
cards.back: A campaign can relate to multiple flows, but each flow relates to only one campaign. Changing an active flow's campaign causes reporting and data stream issues.
cards.frontHtml: What's the relationship between campaigns and flows?
cards.backHtml: A campaign can relate to multiple flows, but each flow relates to only one campaign. Changing an active flow's campaign causes reporting and data stream issues.

cards.front: What are the three ways to create the first flow in a campaign?
cards.back: Flow trigger (Build Your Own → pick a trigger), flow template (goal-driven preconfigured flow), or Quick Start (common use case with preconfigured flow + CMS content).
cards.frontHtml: What are the three ways to create the first flow in a campaign?
cards.backHtml: Flow trigger (Build Your Own → pick a trigger), flow template (goal-driven preconfigured flow), or Quick Start (common use case with preconfigured flow + CMS content).

cards.front: What does the signup form flow template automatically create?
cards.back: A flow, a form, and (optionally) a landing page — all related to the campaign. Lead is the default record type created on submit.
cards.frontHtml: What does the signup form flow template automatically create?

cards.front: What must you do before sending to a segment or previewing membership?
cards.back: Publish the segment first (republish if stale). For the freshest data, republish the segment immediately before running the flow.

cards.front: How does pausing a flow affect Wait elements?
cards.back: The pause duration counts toward the total wait time; past-due tasks complete immediately after resume.
cards.frontHtml: How does pausing a flow affect Wait elements?
cards.backHtml: The pause duration counts toward the total wait time; past-due tasks complete immediately after resume.

cards.front: What are the steps to edit a paused flow?
cards.back: Deactivate (choose "Deactivate and cancel work" or "Deactivate and complete work") → Edit As New Version → Activate. The version number is appended to the flow name.
cards.frontHtml: What are the steps to edit a paused flow?
cards.backHtml: Deactivate (choose "Deactivate and cancel work" or "Deactivate and complete work") → Edit As New Version → Activate. The version number is appended to the flow name.

cards.front: How many exit rules can a flow have, and when are they evaluated?
cards.back: Up to 10; evaluated each time a user starts or resumes a flow. Numeric attributes support aggregation functions (Average, Sum, Max, Min).
cards.frontHtml: How many exit rules can a flow have, and when are they evaluated?
cards.backHtml: Up to 10; evaluated each time a user starts or resumes a flow. Numeric attributes support aggregation functions (Average, Sum, Max, Min).

cards.front: What are the two Decision element logic methods, and how do they differ?
cards.back: Define Manually (outcomes evaluated in order — first match wins) vs. Define with AI (Advanced; all outcomes evaluated simultaneously — order has no impact). AI Decision isn't supported for Marketing Cloud flows.
cards.frontHtml: What are the two Decision element logic methods, and how do they differ?
cards.backHtml: Define Manually (outcomes evaluated in order — first match wins) vs. Define with AI (Advanced; all outcomes evaluated simultaneously — order has no impact). AI Decision isn't supported for Marketing Cloud flows.

cards.front: How does automated Path Experiment selection declare a winner?
cards.back: Bayesian prediction; a path wins at ≥95% confidence to beat all others, otherwise fallback behavior. Percentages are targets, not exact counts (probability-based assignment).
cards.frontHtml: How does automated Path Experiment selection declare a winner?
cards.backHtml: Bayesian prediction; a path wins at ≥95% confidence to beat all others, otherwise fallback behavior. Percentages are targets, not exact counts (probability-based assignment).

cards.front: How do you manually select a winning path, and does it require a new version?
cards.back: Winning Path dropdown on the activated flow — sends all new/remaining/delayed members down that path. It doesn't require saving a new flow version.
cards.frontHtml: How do you manually select a winning path, and does it require a new version?
cards.backHtml: Winning Path dropdown on the activated flow — sends all new/remaining/delayed members down that path. It doesn't require saving a new flow version.

cards.front: What are the Subflow element restrictions?
cards.back: Can't call flows that contain wait elements; variable API names ≤ 40 characters; only flow admins can run inactive flows (others fail at run time if no active version).

cards.front: Which version does a Subflow call by default (API 61.0+)?

cards.front: What happens if you don't set a resume time/time zone on Wait Until Date?

cards.back: Only DMOs categorized as Engagement; only mapped DMOs/fields; related DMOs must be 1:1 or many-to-one; only one related DMO; item identifier required for custom objective-based recommenders.

cards.back: Only the first record; all records; or all records up to a limit between 2 and 20,000. Store all fields, choose fields, or choose fields + assign variables (advanced).

cards.frontHtml: What are the Delete Records warnings?

decks.title: Flashcards — Consent Cache & Subscription Model (MC Next Deep Dive #022)

cards.front: At send time, what is the actual source of truth for consent in Marketing Cloud Next?
cards.back: A cache, not the DMO directly. MC Next checks the cache for a Consent Record matching the recipient's email address; only on a miss does it query the Communication Subscription Consent and populate the cache.
cards.frontHtml: At send time, what is the actual source of truth for consent in Marketing Cloud Next?
cards.backHtml: A cache, not the DMO directly. MC Next checks the cache for a Consent Record matching the recipient's email address; only on a miss does it query the Communication Subscription Consent and populate the cache.

cards.front: What happens on a consent cache miss?
cards.back: The Communication Subscription Consent is queried and the cache populated with that recipient's consent value.
cards.frontHtml: What happens on a consent cache miss?
cards.backHtml: The Communication Subscription Consent is queried and the cache populated with that recipient's consent value.

cards.front: How long is a consent cache value used for?
cards.back: 90 days, unless it is updated through a supported path that refreshes the cache.
cards.frontHtml: How long is a consent cache value used for?
cards.backHtml: 90 days, unless it is updated through a supported path that refreshes the cache.

cards.front: Which consent update methods refresh the consent cache?
cards.back: Manual update from Lead/Contact layouts (Privacy Consent Status LWC), Unsubscribe link / Preference Center, CSV import, and the Create Consent flow activity (official).
cards.frontHtml: Which consent update methods refresh the consent cache?
cards.backHtml: Manual update from Lead/Contact layouts (Privacy Consent Status LWC), Unsubscribe link / Preference Center, CSV import, and the Create Consent flow activity (official).

cards.front: Which Flow activity officially refreshes the consent cache, and which one is not guaranteed?
cards.back: Create Consent is the only officially supported one. MessagingConsentV2.MessagingConsent 'seems' to work but has no official guarantee.
cards.frontHtml: Which Flow activity officially refreshes the consent cache, and which one is not guaranteed?
cards.backHtml: Create Consent is the only officially supported one. MessagingConsentV2.MessagingConsent 'seems' to work but has no official guarantee.

cards.front: What happens if you write consent directly into the Communication Subscription Consent DMO (e.g., via a mapped DLO)?
cards.back: The write does not update the cache, so the new consent can be ignored at send time (stale consent up to the 90-day expiry).
cards.frontHtml: What happens if you write consent directly into the Communication Subscription Consent DMO (e.g., via a mapped DLO)?
cards.backHtml: The write does not update the cache, so the new consent can be ignored at send time (stale consent up to the 90-day expiry).

cards.front: What is the symptom of a stale consent cache?
cards.back: A recipient can keep receiving email even though the CSC DMO shows Opted Out (or a new Opt In may not be honored) until the cache entry is refreshed or expires.
cards.frontHtml: What is the symptom of a stale consent cache?
cards.backHtml: A recipient can keep receiving email even though the CSC DMO shows Opted Out (or a new Opt In may not be honored) until the cache entry is refreshed or expires.

cards.front: How is the primary Id of the Communication Subscription Consent DMO formed?
cards.back: Forged from the Contact Point and the Comm Subscription Channel Type (e.g., contact+002@bamsoo.com#0eBbF00000000HlUAI).
cards.frontHtml: How is the primary Id of the Communication Subscription Consent DMO formed?
cards.backHtml: Forged from the Contact Point and the Comm Subscription Channel Type (e.g., contact+002@bamsoo.com#0eBbF00000000HlUAI).

cards.front: What is MC Next's consent default when no record is found for a Contact Point / Subscription / Channel?
cards.back: Implicit Opt Out — the recipient is assumed opted out.
cards.frontHtml: What is MC Next's consent default when no record is found for a Contact Point / Subscription / Channel?
cards.backHtml: Implicit Opt Out — the recipient is assumed opted out.

cards.front: Which DMO stores the mapping of a Subscription to its Engagement Channels, and how is the combination identified?
cards.back: Communication Subscription Channel Type DMO (CommSubscriptionChannelType Home DSO); each row is a subscription + engagement channel combination, uniquely identified by Comm Subscription Channel Type Id.

cards.front: After Summer '25, why might a Contact Point show 2 consent records for the same Subscription + Channel?
cards.back: The CSC DMO can map to both MessagingConsent and MessagingConsentV2 DSOs. Since Summer '25 only the V2 DSO is written; instances created earlier can have two records, each with a distinct Data Source.

cards.front: When you modify consent and the existing record was created via the V1 system, what happens?
cards.back: The existing V1 record is not updated; a new record is created with V2 as the Data Source. MC Next always uses the latest record as the current Consent Status.

cards.front: How does the Privacy Consent Status component determine what to display?
cards.back: For each Subscription, it checks the CSC DMO for a related record (same Email Address + Subscription, Email Engagement Channel 0eB… ); displays the latest record's status, or Opted Out if none exists (implicit).

cards.front: What does every Promotional Email require, and is there two-click unsubscribe?

cards.front: Why is consent intentionally agnostic of PartyID?
cards.back: A single email/phone can map to multiple individuals (shared household, merges). Keying on the individual would require resolving whose preference "wins"; keying on the address is conservative and regulator-friendly (any opt-out on the address = address opted out).

cards.front: What happens when two people share one email and one opts out?
cards.back: The opt-out affects all of them — there's no way to send to some and suppress others sharing the same address.

decks.title: Flashcards — Consent Objects, Streams & Send-Time Rules (Szymon Lewandowski)

cards.front: What three rules explain almost everything about consent in Marketing Cloud Next?
cards.back: 1) Consent attaches to a contact point value , not a person. 2) No consent record means opted out . 3) At send time the source of truth is a cache , not the record.
cards.frontHtml: What three rules explain almost everything about consent in Marketing Cloud Next?
cards.backHtml: 1) Consent attaches to a contact point value, not a person. 2) No consent record means opted out. 3) At send time the source of truth is a cache, not the record.

cards.front: What does consent attach to in MC Next, and what does it NOT attach to?
cards.back: It attaches to a Contact Point Value (email address, or phone in E.164). It does not attach to an Individual, Unified Individual, or CRM Prospect/Lead/Contact — and it isn't duplicated in CRM.
cards.frontHtml: What does consent attach to in MC Next, and what does it NOT attach to?
cards.backHtml: It attaches to a Contact Point Value (email address, or phone in E.164). It does not attach to an Individual, Unified Individual, or CRM Prospect/Lead/Contact — and it isn't duplicated in CRM.

cards.front: Why does Salesforce key consent on the address rather than the person?
cards.back: When several individuals share a contact point (e.g. office@acme.com ), keying on the person forces the platform to decide whose preference wins. Keying on the address gives the more restrictive default — an opt-out is binding for everyone behind it, which is how regulators look at it.
cards.frontHtml: Why does Salesforce key consent on the address rather than the person?
cards.backHtml: When several individuals share a contact point (e.g. office@acme.com), keying on the person forces the platform to decide whose preference wins. Keying on the address gives the more restrictive default — an opt-out is binding for everyone behind it, which is how regulators look at it.

cards.front: What happens to consent when someone changes their email address?
cards.back: Their consent is stranded on the old address . The new address has no record, which means opted out .
cards.frontHtml: What happens to consent when someone changes their email address?
cards.backHtml: Their consent is stranded on the old address. The new address has no record, which means opted out.

cards.front: What happens to the consent record when you delete the Contact?
cards.back: The consent record stays in Data 360 , keyed to an address that no longer appears anywhere in your CRM.
cards.frontHtml: What happens to the consent record when you delete the Contact?
cards.backHtml: The consent record stays in Data 360, keyed to an address that no longer appears anywhere in your CRM.

cards.front: On the day you switch Marketing Cloud Next on, what is the consent state of your existing database?
cards.back: Entirely opted out — no consent record means opt-out, so the whole base starts suppressed until you import consent.
cards.frontHtml: On the day you switch Marketing Cloud Next on, what is the consent state of your existing database?
cards.backHtml: Entirely opted out — no consent record means opt-out, so the whole base starts suppressed until you import consent.

cards.front: Can you drive commercial sends from custom flag fields on Contact or Lead?
cards.back: No. There is no supported path. Custom flags can feed the standard model through a flow, but they cannot replace it — updating those objects alone does nothing at send time.

cards.back: Eight — each file covers exactly one channel, one subscription and one status (2 subscriptions × 2 channels × 2 statuses).

cards.back: Only two — opt-in and opt-out, nothing in between. The CRM CommSubscriptionConsent object (the empty one) carries OptInPending / OptOutPending since API 58.0 — every state a double opt-in flow could want, on the object that has no bearing on sends.

cards.front: How does SMS/WhatsApp/RCS opt-out granularity differ from email?
cards.back: Each SMS code, WhatsApp number and RCS agent maps to one or more subscriptions , and opting out of the channel opts the person out of every subscription mapped to it . There is no per-subscription opt-out over SMS.
cards.frontHtml: How does SMS/WhatsApp/RCS opt-out granularity differ from email?
cards.backHtml: Each SMS code, WhatsApp number and RCS agent maps to one or more subscriptions, and opting out of the channel opts the person out of every subscription mapped to it. There is no per-subscription opt-out over SMS.

cards.front: What is the one exception to the one-channel-one-consent rule?
cards.back: RCS — Salesforce says you can reuse existing SMS consent when the messaging use case stays the same, and tells you to check that with your legal team.
cards.frontHtml: What is the one exception to the one-channel-one-consent rule?
cards.backHtml: RCS — Salesforce says you can reuse existing SMS consent when the messaging use case stays the same, and tells you to check that with your legal team.

cards.front: How do Compliance BCC and CC recipients behave with consent checks?
cards.back: Compliance BCC is excluded from consent checks entirely (it doesn't represent a person). CC recipients are suppressed if the primary recipient doesn't get the email because the address lacks consent.
cards.frontHtml: How do Compliance BCC and CC recipients behave with consent checks?
cards.backHtml: Compliance BCC is excluded from consent checks entirely (it doesn't represent a person). CC recipients are suppressed if the primary recipient doesn't get the email because the address lacks consent.

cards.front: What are the three consent models in Salesforce, and which does MC Next read?
cards.back: 1) Salesforce Consent Data Model (legal basis). 2) Data 360 consent objects (activation eligibility). 3) Communication Subscription Consent (MC Next sends). MC Next reads only the third , through the cache.
cards.frontHtml: What are the three consent models in Salesforce, and which does MC Next read?
cards.backHtml: 1) Salesforce Consent Data Model (legal basis). 2) Data 360 consent objects (activation eligibility). 3) Communication Subscription Consent (MC Next sends). MC Next reads only the third, through the cache.

cards.front: Name the four consent objects and the Id prefixes of the first three.
cards.back: Communication Subscription ( 0Xl ), Engagement Channel Type ( 0eF ), Communication Subscription Channel Type ( 0eB ), Communication Subscription Consent (no prefix). The first three are CRM objects ; the consent record lives in Data 360 only .
cards.frontHtml: Name the four consent objects and the Id prefixes of the first three.
cards.backHtml: Communication Subscription (0Xl), Engagement Channel Type (0eF), Communication Subscription Channel Type (0eB), Communication Subscription Consent (no prefix). The first three are CRM objects; the consent record lives in Data 360 only.

cards.front: Since which API version have CommSubscription and CommSubscriptionConsent existed?
cards.back: API 48.0 (Spring '20) — roughly five years before Marketing Cloud Next existed.
cards.frontHtml: Since which API version have CommSubscription and CommSubscriptionConsent existed?
cards.backHtml: API 48.0 (Spring '20) — roughly five years before Marketing Cloud Next existed.

cards.front: Does Engagement Channel Type have a DMO?
cards.back: No. Communication Subscription Channel Type carries an ssot EngagementChannelTypeId c with no relationship attached — on the Data 360 side the channel is a bare identifier pointing nowhere.
cards.frontHtml: Does Engagement Channel Type have a DMO?
cards.backHtml: No. Communication Subscription Channel Type carries an ssot__EngagementChannelTypeId__c with no relationship attached — on the Data 360 side the channel is a bare identifier pointing nowhere.

cards.front: Can you change a subscription's scope after creation?
cards.back: No. With business units (Advanced), a subscription is assigned to a single BU or all BUs, and the scope cannot be edited after creation . It also limits which channels you can add.
cards.frontHtml: Can you change a subscription's scope after creation?
cards.backHtml: No. With business units (Advanced), a subscription is assigned to a single BU or all BUs, and the scope cannot be edited after creation. It also limits which channels you can add.

cards.front: What happens when you delete a Communication Subscription?
cards.back: It deletes all of its consent data — a legal exposure, not just an admin inconvenience. Salesforce's recommendation is simply not to delete subscriptions once consent has been collected.
cards.frontHtml: What happens when you delete a Communication Subscription?
cards.backHtml: It deletes all of its consent data — a legal exposure, not just an admin inconvenience. Salesforce's recommendation is simply not to delete subscriptions once consent has been collected.

cards.front: Does a new subscription automatically appear on the preference page?
cards.back: No. MC Next ships one customizable email preference page containing only the default marketing subscription. Adding subscriptions to it is a separate step after creation.
cards.frontHtml: Does a new subscription automatically appear on the preference page?
cards.backHtml: No. MC Next ships one customizable email preference page containing only the default marketing subscription. Adding subscriptions to it is a separate step after creation.

cards.front: Does MC Next support frequency capping on a subscription?
cards.back: No. The platform has a CommSubscriptionTiming object for exactly this, but MC Next doesn't map it . Send-frequency rules live in your journey logic or segment.
cards.frontHtml: Does MC Next support frequency capping on a subscription?
cards.backHtml: No. The platform has a CommSubscriptionTiming object for exactly this, but MC Next doesn't map it. Send-frequency rules live in your journey logic or segment.

cards.front: What is the whole join key for a consent record, and what does it make possible/impossible?
cards.back: Contact point value + Communication Subscription Channel Type Id . Searching consent by email address works ; searching it by person doesn't . The consent DMO has exactly one traversable relationship (N:1 to CSCT).
cards.frontHtml: What is the whole join key for a consent record, and what does it make possible/impossible?
cards.backHtml: Contact point value + Communication Subscription Channel Type Id. Searching consent by email address works; searching it by person doesn't. The consent DMO has exactly one traversable relationship (N:1 to CSCT).

cards.front: What is the state of the Party field on the consent DMO?
cards.back: It's an out-of-the-box relationship between Individual.Id and CommunicationSubscriptionConsent.Party , wired end to end from the DLO — and always empty . Never build on it.
cards.frontHtml: What is the state of the Party field on the consent DMO?
cards.backHtml: It's an out-of-the-box relationship between Individual.Id and CommunicationSubscriptionConsent.Party, wired end to end from the DLO — and always empty. Never build on it.

cards.front: How do you correctly join a consent record back to a person?
cards.back: Through the Contact Point Email or Contact Point Phone DMO (which carry the PartyId mapping), matching on the contact point value — the same way the Privacy Consent Status component does it.
cards.frontHtml: How do you correctly join a consent record back to a person?
cards.backHtml: Through the Contact Point Email or Contact Point Phone DMO (which carry the PartyId mapping), matching on the contact point value — the same way the Privacy Consent Status component does it.

cards.front: What are the two namespaces of the consent DMO, and why does it matter?
cards.back: The older ssot CommunicationSubscriptionConsent dlm and the newer std CommunicationSubscriptionConsentDmo dlm (API version 254). Their field lists are not identical — the public reference for the older one lists ssot ContactPointId c and no contact point value field at all .
cards.frontHtml: What are the two namespaces of the consent DMO, and why does it matter?
cards.backHtml: The older ssot__CommunicationSubscriptionConsent__dlm and the newer std__CommunicationSubscriptionConsentDmo__dlm (API version 254). Their field lists are not identical — the public reference for the older one lists ssot__ContactPointId__c and no contact point value field at all.

cards.front: What is the name of the data kit that carries consent, and how many streams does it install?
cards.back: UnifiedMessagingConsent — it installs two data streams: one for the consent records ( MessagingConsentV2 ) and one for the audit trail ( ConsentAuditTrailV2 ).
cards.frontHtml: What is the name of the data kit that carries consent, and how many streams does it install?
cards.backHtml: UnifiedMessagingConsent — it installs two data streams: one for the consent records (MessagingConsentV2) and one for the audit trail (ConsentAuditTrailV2).

cards.front: What are the two ways an org ends up with duplicate consent records for the same contact point and subscription?
cards.back: 1) The documented generation switch (pre-Summer '25 orgs moved MessagingConsent → MessagingConsentV2 ). 2) The org-ID naming quirk — Salesforce appended the org ID to stream names, both spellings stayed active, so even a V2-only org gets duplicates.
cards.frontHtml: What are the two ways an org ends up with duplicate consent records for the same contact point and subscription?
