cards.front: What three areas does the final session cover?
cards.back: 1) How contact point resolution works at send time. 2) Agentforce and other AI-powered innovations . 3) Analytics and performance insight reports and dashboards.
cards.frontHtml: What three areas does the final session cover?
cards.backHtml: 1) How contact point resolution works at send time. 2) Agentforce and other AI-powered innovations. 3) Analytics and performance insight reports and dashboards.

cards.front: How does the contact point model differ between MCE and Data 360?
cards.back: MCE subscribers can only have one email address . In Data 360, an individual can have multiple email addresses , plus multiple contact point values for other channels like SMS.
cards.frontHtml: How does the contact point model differ between MCE and Data 360?
cards.backHtml: MCE subscribers can only have one email address. In Data 360, an individual can have multiple email addresses, plus multiple contact point values for other channels like SMS.

cards.front: Do reconciliation rules determine which contact point is used?
cards.back: ⚠️ No. Reconciliation rules determine which single value is selected for a unified field that can't contain multiple values (like an individual's name). They don't apply to contact points such as email addresses or phone numbers.
cards.frontHtml: Do reconciliation rules determine which contact point is used?
cards.backHtml: ⚠️ No. Reconciliation rules determine which single value is selected for a unified field that can't contain multiple values (like an individual's name). They don't apply to contact points such as email addresses or phone numbers.

cards.front: What happens to all contact points after identity resolution?
cards.back: They are all retained as part of the unified profile and remain available for segmentation and activation .
cards.frontHtml: What happens to all contact points after identity resolution?
cards.backHtml: They are all retained as part of the unified profile and remain available for segmentation and activation.

cards.front: If a unified individual has records with three email addresses, two of which are the same, how many emails are sent?
cards.back: Two — a separate message is sent to each unique email address , and a duplicate address is treated as a single contact point (one send).
cards.frontHtml: If a unified individual has records with three email addresses, two of which are the same, how many emails are sent?
cards.backHtml: Two — a separate message is sent to each unique email address, and a duplicate address is treated as a single contact point (one send).

cards.front: Name the four ways MC Next determines which contact point to use at send time.
cards.back: 1) Data graph selected in the flow's automation properties. 2) On-demand flow API payload . 3) Activation source priority order (activation-triggered flows). 4) Activation template (audience flows using a segment).
cards.frontHtml: Name the four ways MC Next determines which contact point to use at send time.
cards.backHtml: 1) Data graph selected in the flow's automation properties. 2) On-demand flow API payload. 3) Activation source priority order (activation-triggered flows). 4) Activation template (audience flows using a segment).

cards.front: What must the flow's data graph include for contact point selection to work?
cards.back: A specific structure and field set — otherwise messages won't send successfully. (The required structure is documented on a Salesforce Help page.)
cards.frontHtml: What must the flow's data graph include for contact point selection to work?
cards.backHtml: A specific structure and field set — otherwise messages won't send successfully. (The required structure is documented on a Salesforce Help page.)

cards.front: In an on-demand flow, what takes precedence — the API payload or a configured data graph?
cards.back: The contact point is typically derived from the API payload , but if a data graph is configured in the flow's automation properties, that data graph takes precedence .
cards.frontHtml: In an on-demand flow, what takes precedence — the API payload or a configured data graph?
cards.backHtml: The contact point is typically derived from the API payload, but if a data graph is configured in the flow's automation properties, that data graph takes precedence.

cards.front: What is an activation template?
cards.back: A template that lets you define the source priority order and use rules to filter the segment members or contact points included in an activation. You select it when configuring a send message element in a flow.
cards.frontHtml: What is an activation template?
cards.backHtml: A template that lets you define the source priority order and use rules to filter the segment members or contact points included in an activation. You select it when configuring a send message element in a flow.

cards.front: When is an activation template required?
cards.back: When the segment's segment-on object is NOT Unified Individual .
cards.frontHtml: When is an activation template required?
cards.backHtml: When the segment's segment-on object is NOT Unified Individual.

cards.front: Walk through creating an activation template.
cards.back: Activations tab in Data 360 → New → select Template as the activation type → Continue → select a data space and the DMO used as the segment-on criteria (typically Individual or Unified Individual) → choose Data Cloud as the platform → Continue → define the priority order for contact point selection (expand the email channel → Edit ) → Save → optionally add contact point filters and activation membership filters → name and save.
cards.frontHtml: Walk through creating an activation template.
cards.backHtml: Activations tab in Data 360 → New → select Template as the activation type → Continue → select a data space and the DMO used as the segment-on criteria (typically Individual or Unified Individual) → choose Data Cloud as the platform → Continue → define the priority order for contact point selection (expand the email channel → Edit) → Save → optionally add contact point filters and activation membership filters → name and save.

cards.front: In the demo, what source priority order was configured, and what's the result?
cards.back: Salesforce → Contact , then Salesforce → Lead , then Any (all other sources). MC Next prioritises an email from a Contact record; if unavailable, a Lead record; then any other source .
cards.frontHtml: In the demo, what source priority order was configured, and what's the result?
cards.backHtml: Salesforce → Contact, then Salesforce → Lead, then Any (all other sources). MC Next prioritises an email from a Contact record; if unavailable, a Lead record; then any other source.

cards.front: Which DMO holds the telephone number field for phone contact point selection?
cards.back: The Contact Point Phone DMO — not the Individual or Unified Individual DMO.
cards.frontHtml: Which DMO holds the telephone number field for phone contact point selection?
cards.backHtml: The Contact Point Phone DMO — not the Individual or Unified Individual DMO.

cards.front: Name the five out-of-the-box AI agents in Marketing Cloud Next.
cards.back: Segment Creation Agent , Campaign Creation Agent , Content Creation Agent , Journey Decisioning Agent , and Account Discovery Agent .
cards.frontHtml: Name the five out-of-the-box AI agents in Marketing Cloud Next.
cards.backHtml: Segment Creation Agent, Campaign Creation Agent, Content Creation Agent, Journey Decisioning Agent, and Account Discovery Agent.

cards.front: What does the Segment Creation Agent do?
cards.back: Uses natural language prompts to create Data 360 audience segments — translating an audience description into editable segmentation criteria .
cards.frontHtml: What does the Segment Creation Agent do?
cards.backHtml: Uses natural language prompts to create Data 360 audience segments — translating an audience description into editable segmentation criteria.

cards.front: What does the Campaign Creation Agent do?
cards.back: Creates campaign briefs, flows, and multi-channel content from conversational prompts — accelerating campaign planning and development.
cards.frontHtml: What does the Campaign Creation Agent do?
cards.backHtml: Creates campaign briefs, flows, and multi-channel content from conversational prompts — accelerating campaign planning and development.

cards.front: What does the Content Creation Agent do?
cards.back: Drafts and refines content for emails, landing pages, and SMS messages — adjusting messaging, tone, length, or audience relevance.
cards.frontHtml: What does the Content Creation Agent do?
cards.backHtml: Drafts and refines content for emails, landing pages, and SMS messages — adjusting messaging, tone, length, or audience relevance.

cards.front: What does the Journey Decisioning Agent do?
cards.back: Selects the most appropriate journey or flow and creates personalized content for each individual.
cards.frontHtml: What does the Journey Decisioning Agent do?
cards.backHtml: Selects the most appropriate journey or flow and creates personalized content for each individual.

cards.front: What does the Account Discovery Agent do?
cards.back: Provides account insights and identifies potential buying group members — helping discover stakeholders and guide nurturing or follow-up activities.
cards.frontHtml: What does the Account Discovery Agent do?
cards.backHtml: Provides account insights and identifies potential buying group members — helping discover stakeholders and guide nurturing or follow-up activities.

cards.front: Walk through the "Draft with Agentforce" campaign flow.
cards.back: Marketing Home → New Campaign → Draft with Agentforce → describe the campaign objective → choose to draft a brief → ask Agentforce to generate a campaign → Agentforce creates a draft campaign brief → open the campaign preview (flow + content) → save as a new campaign → open the campaign record.
cards.frontHtml: Walk through the "Draft with Agentforce" campaign flow.
cards.backHtml: Marketing Home → New Campaign → Draft with Agentforce → describe the campaign objective → choose to draft a brief → ask Agentforce to generate a campaign → Agentforce creates a draft campaign brief → open the campaign preview (flow + content) → save as a new campaign → open the campaign record.

cards.front: How does Einstein Segment Creation fit into the campaign demo?
cards.back: Select Segment → Segment Builder → Next → Create with Einstein Segment Creation → choose the DMO → Next . Einstein has already drafted an audience definition based on the campaign objective ; you can refine it or edit rules manually, then Create Segment .
cards.frontHtml: How does Einstein Segment Creation fit into the campaign demo?
cards.backHtml: Select Segment → Segment Builder → Next → Create with Einstein Segment Creation → choose the DMO → Next. Einstein has already drafted an audience definition based on the campaign objective; you can refine it or edit rules manually, then Create Segment.

cards.front: Name the three predictive AI capabilities in MC Next, and which are Advanced-only?
cards.back: Engagement Frequency , Engagement Scoring , and Send Time Optimization . ⚠️ Engagement Frequency and Engagement Scoring are Advanced only — not Growth.
cards.frontHtml: Name the three predictive AI capabilities in MC Next, and which are Advanced-only?
cards.backHtml: Engagement Frequency, Engagement Scoring, and Send Time Optimization. ⚠️ Engagement Frequency and Engagement Scoring are Advanced only — not Growth.

cards.front: How do you use predictive AI insights for segmentation and decisioning?
cards.back: Configure the required data graph first, then use fields like Email Engagement Frequency or Engagement Score to create branches with a Decision element — or use those DMO fields as segment criteria .
cards.frontHtml: How do you use predictive AI insights for segmentation and decisioning?
cards.backHtml: Configure the required data graph first, then use fields like Email Engagement Frequency or Engagement Score to create branches with a Decision element — or use those DMO fields as segment criteria.

cards.front: What is the goal of Engagement Frequency?
cards.back: To determine how often each contact should receive an email — maximising engagement while reducing email fatigue and unsubscribes .
cards.frontHtml: What is the goal of Engagement Frequency?
cards.backHtml: To determine how often each contact should receive an email — maximising engagement while reducing email fatigue and unsubscribes.

cards.front: What does Engagement Frequency analyse, and how is it trained?
cards.back: Up to 90 days of email activity — sends, opens, clicks, bounces, unsubscribes, spam complaints, and sending patterns . It compares each individual's behaviour at different frequencies with similar individuals , then calculates an ideal frequency range . ⚠️ Trained only on your org's data ; scores refreshed weekly .
cards.frontHtml: What does Engagement Frequency analyse, and how is it trained?
cards.backHtml: Up to 90 days of email activity — sends, opens, clicks, bounces, unsubscribes, spam complaints, and sending patterns. It compares each individual's behaviour at different frequencies with similar individuals, then calculates an ideal frequency range. ⚠️ Trained only on your org's data; scores refreshed weekly.

cards.front: What are the four Engagement Frequency classifications?
cards.back: The Email Engagement Classification field in the Email Engagement Frequency DMO assigns each individual to: Saturated · Almost Saturated · On Target · Under Saturated .
cards.frontHtml: What are the four Engagement Frequency classifications?
cards.backHtml: The Email Engagement Classification field in the Email Engagement Frequency DMO assigns each individual to: Saturated · Almost Saturated · On Target · Under Saturated.

cards.front: What does Engagement Scoring estimate?
cards.back: How likely each individual is to engage with future marketing communications .
cards.frontHtml: What does Engagement Scoring estimate?
cards.backHtml: How likely each individual is to engage with future marketing communications.

cards.front: What does Engagement Scoring analyse?
cards.back: Up to 90 days of historical behaviour, placing greater emphasis on the most recent activity — email sends, opens, clicks, bounces, unsubscribes, subscription history , and website interactions .
cards.frontHtml: What does Engagement Scoring analyse?
cards.backHtml: Up to 90 days of historical behaviour, placing greater emphasis on the most recent activity — email sends, opens, clicks, bounces, unsubscribes, subscription history, and website interactions.

cards.front: What three likelihood predictions does Engagement Scoring generate?
cards.back: Likelihood to open an email, likelihood to click a link, and likelihood to remain subscribed .
cards.frontHtml: What three likelihood predictions does Engagement Scoring generate?
cards.backHtml: Likelihood to open an email, likelihood to click a link, and likelihood to remain subscribed.

cards.front: Name the four Engagement Scoring personas and their open/click likelihoods.
cards.back: Loyalists (high open, high click) · Selective Subscribers (low open, high click) · Window Shoppers (high open, low click) · Win Back / Dormant (low open, low click).
cards.frontHtml: Name the four Engagement Scoring personas and their open/click likelihoods.
cards.backHtml: Loyalists (high open, high click) · Selective Subscribers (low open, high click) · Window Shoppers (high open, low click) · Win Back / Dormant (low open, low click).

cards.front: How might you use the Engagement Scoring personas?
cards.back: Send surveys to understand selective subscribers, engage window shoppers via alternative channels , and place dormant subscribers into a dedicated win-back campaign .
cards.frontHtml: How might you use the Engagement Scoring personas?
cards.backHtml: Send surveys to understand selective subscribers, engage window shoppers via alternative channels, and place dormant subscribers into a dedicated win-back campaign.

cards.front: What four tiers are the likelihood predictions grouped into?
cards.back: Most Likely · More Likely · Less Likely · Least Likely — usable in a Decision element to route individuals along different flow paths.
cards.frontHtml: What four tiers are the likelihood predictions grouped into?
cards.backHtml: Most Likely · More Likely · Less Likely · Least Likely — usable in a Decision element to route individuals along different flow paths.

cards.front: What does Send Time Optimization do?
cards.back: Determines when each individual is most likely to engage with an email — rather than sending to everyone at the same time.
cards.frontHtml: What does Send Time Optimization do?
cards.backHtml: Determines when each individual is most likely to engage with an email — rather than sending to everyone at the same time.

cards.front: What does STO analyse, and how often are predictions updated?
cards.back: Up to 90 days of email engagement history — sends, opens, clicks, bounces, unsubscribes, spam complaints, plus the timestamps of those events. Predictions update approximately once a week .
cards.frontHtml: What does STO analyse, and how often are predictions updated?
cards.backHtml: Up to 90 days of email engagement history — sends, opens, clicks, bounces, unsubscribes, spam complaints, plus the timestamps of those events. Predictions update approximately once a week.

cards.front: Which editions support STO, and what setup is required?
cards.back: Both Growth and Advanced editions, and it must be enabled in Setup . Add the Send Time Optimization DMO to your data graph (required structure), then select the Hourly Scores by Week field.
cards.frontHtml: Which editions support STO, and what setup is required?
cards.backHtml: Both Growth and Advanced editions, and it must be enabled in Setup. Add the Send Time Optimization DMO to your data graph (required structure), then select the Hourly Scores by Week field.

cards.front: What is the STO optimization window range?
cards.back: From 2 hours up to 1 week . MC Next sends each message at the recipient's predicted optimal time within that window.
cards.frontHtml: What is the STO optimization window range?
cards.backHtml: From 2 hours up to 1 week. MC Next sends each message at the recipient's predicted optimal time within that window.

cards.front: Name the three out-of-the-box reporting capabilities and what each provides.
cards.back: Campaign Performance Dashboard (end-to-end view of an individual campaign — sends, opens, clicks, bounces, contact progression) · Marketing Performance Dashboard (broader cross-channel view over time — audience growth, program-level engagement trends) · Semantic Data Model (consistent business layer for custom reports, stakeholder sharing, and external tool connections). ⚠️ All three are included with no additional license or SKU .
cards.frontHtml: Name the three out-of-the-box reporting capabilities and what each provides.
cards.backHtml: Campaign Performance Dashboard (end-to-end view of an individual campaign — sends, opens, clicks, bounces, contact progression) · Marketing Performance Dashboard (broader cross-channel view over time — audience growth, program-level engagement trends) · Semantic Data Model (consistent business layer for custom reports, stakeholder sharing, and external tool connections). ⚠️ All three are included with no additional license or SKU.

cards.front: Where are marketing performance dashboards available, and what do they show?
cards.back: From the Marketing Analytics tab . They give a consolidated view across marketing activities — overall campaign engagement and top-performing campaigns, audience segments, content, and channels — bringing together web, email, SMS, WhatsApp, and mobile .
cards.frontHtml: Where are marketing performance dashboards available, and what do they show?
cards.backHtml: From the Marketing Analytics tab. They give a consolidated view across marketing activities — overall campaign engagement and top-performing campaigns, audience segments, content, and channels — bringing together web, email, SMS, WhatsApp, and mobile.

cards.front: Where else do the performance dashboards appear?
cards.back: Embedded directly in each campaign record , so you can evaluate an individual campaign's results in context without navigating to a separate reporting tab.
cards.frontHtml: Where else do the performance dashboards appear?
cards.backHtml: Embedded directly in each campaign record, so you can evaluate an individual campaign's results in context without navigating to a separate reporting tab.

cards.front: How do you access content performance dashboards?
cards.back: Select the corresponding element in your active flow (e.g., a Send Email Message element) → from the Analytics tab click Details → review pulse card metrics for the content type plus row-level data .
cards.frontHtml: How do you access content performance dashboards?
cards.backHtml: Select the corresponding element in your active flow (e.g., a Send Email Message element) → from the Analytics tab click Details → review pulse card metrics for the content type plus row-level data.

cards.front: What do the deliverability dashboards cover, and what are they for?
cards.back: SMS, WhatsApp, and mobile app messaging . They provide visibility into message delivery health and campaign performance, and help you understand why a message failed to reach specific recipients .
cards.frontHtml: What do the deliverability dashboards cover, and what are they for?
cards.backHtml: SMS, WhatsApp, and mobile app messaging. They provide visibility into message delivery health and campaign performance, and help you understand why a message failed to reach specific recipients.

cards.front: What is the semantic data model, and what does it do?
cards.back: Powered by Tableau Next , it's the foundation for reports and dashboards in MC Next, available from the Analytics tab . The Marketing Intelligence Semantic Data Model combines data from multiple Data 360 objects and defines the relationships and metrics for campaign performance, engagement, and deliverability — applied centrally so metrics calculate consistently .
cards.frontHtml: What is the semantic data model, and what does it do?
cards.backHtml: Powered by Tableau Next, it's the foundation for reports and dashboards in MC Next, available from the Analytics tab. The Marketing Intelligence Semantic Data Model combines data from multiple Data 360 objects and defines the relationships and metrics for campaign performance, engagement, and deliverability — applied centrally so metrics calculate consistently.

cards.front: What can you do with the semantic data model?
cards.back: Create reports answering specific business questions, combine them as widgets in a dashboard , customise standard dashboards (widgets, labels, layouts, filters), extend it to other Data 360 objects, build custom reports , share data with stakeholders outside Salesforce CRM , or connect any external tool .
cards.frontHtml: What can you do with the semantic data model?
cards.backHtml: Create reports answering specific business questions, combine them as widgets in a dashboard, customise standard dashboards (widgets, labels, layouts, filters), extend it to other Data 360 objects, build custom reports, share data with stakeholders outside Salesforce CRM, or connect any external tool.

cards.front: What is the Unified Engagement History dashboard?
cards.back: A pre-built dashboard giving sales and marketing teams a shared view of activities performed by the leads and contacts associated with an account . Sales reps use it to identify the most engaged people , understand their interests, and decide who to contact next . Powered by Data 360 and Tableau Next .
cards.frontHtml: What is the Unified Engagement History dashboard?
cards.backHtml: A pre-built dashboard giving sales and marketing teams a shared view of activities performed by the leads and contacts associated with an account. Sales reps use it to identify the most engaged people, understand their interests, and decide who to contact next. Powered by Data 360 and Tableau Next.

cards.front: How do you embed the Unified Engagement History dashboard?
cards.back: Add the Unified Engagement History dashboard component to the page layout of account, lead, and contact records.
cards.frontHtml: How do you embed the Unified Engagement History dashboard?
cards.backHtml: Add the Unified Engagement History dashboard component to the page layout of account, lead, and contact records.

decks.title: Flashcards — Identity Resolution, Billing & Flow Orchestration

cards.front: How do match rules vs. match criteria affect consolidation rate?
cards.back: More match rules = higher consolidation (more match opportunities); more criteria per rule = lower consolidation (harder to match).
cards.frontHtml: How do match rules vs. match criteria affect consolidation rate?
cards.backHtml: More match rules = higher consolidation (more match opportunities); more criteria per rule = lower consolidation (harder to match).

cards.front: Name the five match methods.
cards.back: Exact, Exact Normalized, Fuzzy - High Precision, Fuzzy - Medium Precision, Fuzzy - Low Precision.
cards.frontHtml: Name the five match methods.
cards.backHtml: Exact, Exact Normalized, Fuzzy - High Precision, Fuzzy - Medium Precision, Fuzzy - Low Precision.

cards.front: What AI model powers fuzzy matching, and what's its confidence threshold?
cards.back: BERT language model trained on 150+ countries, 3B English words, 20M names; 0.7 confidence threshold.
cards.frontHtml: What AI model powers fuzzy matching, and what's its confidence threshold?
cards.backHtml: BERT language model trained on 150+ countries, 3B English words, 20M names; 0.7 confidence threshold.

cards.front: How does real-time matching differ from scheduled matching?
cards.back: In real-time, all criteria except phone/email run Exact; phone and email run Exact Normalized (unless Exact was the scheduled method).
cards.frontHtml: How does real-time matching differ from scheduled matching?
cards.backHtml: In real-time, all criteria except phone/email run Exact; phone and email run Exact Normalized (unless Exact was the scheduled method).

cards.front: What's the risk of Match on Blank, and when is it ignored?
cards.back: Can cause overmatching (e.g., middle name) and the "matched 50,000+ profiles" error; it's ignored in real-time matching.
cards.frontHtml: What's the risk of Match on Blank, and when is it ignored?
cards.backHtml: Can cause overmatching (e.g., middle name) and the "matched 50,000+ profiles" error; it's ignored in real-time matching.

cards.front: Why isn't matching on a single contact point recommended?
cards.back: It can mix household members sharing an email/phone into a single unified profile (except unique external identifiers like party ID).
cards.frontHtml: Why isn't matching on a single contact point recommended?
cards.backHtml: It can mix household members sharing an email/phone into a single unified profile (except unique external identifiers like party ID).

cards.front: What are the four default match rules for individuals?
cards.back: Fuzzy Name + Normalized Email; Fuzzy Name + Normalized Phone; Fuzzy Name + Normalized Address; Fuzzy Name + Normalized Phone + Normalized Email.
cards.frontHtml: What are the four default match rules for individuals?
cards.backHtml: Fuzzy Name + Normalized Email; Fuzzy Name + Normalized Phone; Fuzzy Name + Normalized Address; Fuzzy Name + Normalized Phone + Normalized Email.

cards.front: How many match rules can a household ruleset have?
cards.back: Only one. Recommended: last name + address, or party identifier.
cards.frontHtml: How many match rules can a household ruleset have?
cards.backHtml: Only one. Recommended: last name + address, or party identifier.

cards.front: When is a unified profile considered known vs anonymous?
cards.back: Known if any source profile was designated known; anonymous if only anonymous sources. Account profiles are always known.
cards.frontHtml: When is a unified profile considered known vs anonymous?
cards.backHtml: Known if any source profile was designated known; anonymous if only anonymous sources. Account profiles are always known.

cards.front: What are the three reconciliation rule types?
cards.back: Last Updated, Most Frequent, Source Priority.
cards.frontHtml: What are the three reconciliation rule types?
cards.backHtml: Last Updated, Most Frequent, Source Priority.

cards.front: Do reconciliation rules apply to contact points?
cards.back: No — they only reconcile Unified Individual object fields. Use source priority order in activations to deliver contact points.
cards.frontHtml: Do reconciliation rules apply to contact points?
cards.backHtml: No — they only reconcile Unified Individual object fields. Use source priority order in activations to deliver contact points.

cards.front: Which reconciliation rule should you use on ID fields, and why?
cards.back: Source Priority — to stabilize ID values.
cards.frontHtml: Which reconciliation rule should you use on ID fields, and why?
cards.backHtml: Source Priority — to stabilize ID values.

cards.front: Does ingesting via the internal Salesforce connector consume credits?
cards.back: No — free as of Aug 7, 2025 (included with Data 360). External ingestion consumes credits.
cards.frontHtml: Does ingesting via the internal Salesforce connector consume credits?
cards.backHtml: No — free as of Aug 7, 2025 (included with Data 360). External ingestion consumes credits.

cards.front: When does Activate DMO - Streaming double the records processed?
cards.back: When a data graph is used with the activation (1 record change = 2 records processed).
cards.frontHtml: When does Activate DMO - Streaming double the records processed?
cards.backHtml: When a data graph is used with the activation (1 record change = 2 records processed).

cards.front: When does a Batch Calculated Insight charge credits?
cards.back: Only when underlying objects change; no charge if no changes. Objects used multiple times counted once.
cards.frontHtml: When does a Batch Calculated Insight charge credits?
cards.backHtml: Only when underlying objects change; no charge if no changes. Objects used multiple times counted once.

cards.front: How is Batch Profile Unification billed after the first run?
cards.back: Only new or modified source profiles count (deleted or suppressed profiles count as modified).
cards.frontHtml: How is Batch Profile Unification billed after the first run?
cards.backHtml: Only new or modified source profiles count (deleted or suppressed profiles count as modified).

cards.front: What's the minimum credit decrement per usage type?
cards.back: 1 credit, where fractional usage amounts to 1+ credits over the monthly billing period.
cards.frontHtml: What's the minimum credit decrement per usage type?
cards.backHtml: 1 credit, where fractional usage amounts to 1+ credits over the monthly billing period.

cards.front: In which flow type is the Create Consent element available?
cards.back: Automation Event-Triggered flows only (per the marketing flow elements table).
cards.frontHtml: In which flow type is the Create Consent element available?
cards.backHtml: Automation Event-Triggered flows only (per the marketing flow elements table).

cards.front: What edition + add-on do Path Experiments require?
cards.back: Advanced edition + Personalization.
cards.frontHtml: What edition + add-on do Path Experiments require?
cards.backHtml: Advanced edition + Personalization.

cards.front: Which edition supports On-Canvas Insights?
cards.back: Advanced only.
cards.frontHtml: Which edition supports On-Canvas Insights?
cards.backHtml: Advanced only.

cards.front: Is a paused flow considered active?
cards.back: Yes — a paused flow counts as active, so only one version can be active.
cards.frontHtml: Is a paused flow considered active?
cards.backHtml: Yes — a paused flow counts as active, so only one version can be active.

cards.front: Which activation target type do activation-triggered flows support?
cards.back: Only Data 360 activation target type; other target types error on save.
cards.frontHtml: Which activation target type do activation-triggered flows support?
cards.backHtml: Only Data 360 activation target type; other target types error on save.

cards.front: What's the concurrency limit for Marketing Cloud/Data 360 activation-triggered flows?
cards.back: 15,000,000 actions/hour with 210 concurrent threads.
cards.frontHtml: What's the concurrency limit for Marketing Cloud/Data 360 activation-triggered flows?
cards.backHtml: 15,000,000 actions/hour with 210 concurrent threads.

cards.front: What error-rate threshold triggers additional rate limiting?
cards.back: Elements failing more than 2.5% of the time.
cards.frontHtml: What error-rate threshold triggers additional rate limiting?
cards.backHtml: Elements failing more than 2.5% of the time.

cards.front: What allowance do real-time-response flows get?
cards.back: 50% additional allowance to the concurrency limit (e.g., 210 → 315).
cards.frontHtml: What allowance do real-time-response flows get?
cards.backHtml: 50% additional allowance to the concurrency limit (e.g., 210 → 315).

cards.front: What are the four audience sources for an audience flow?
cards.back: Segment, List, Record, Campaign.
cards.frontHtml: What are the four audience sources for an audience flow?
cards.backHtml: Segment, List, Record, Campaign.

cards.front: What type of segment do broadcast flows use?
cards.back: Dynamic segments — membership is determined after the flow starts.
cards.frontHtml: What type of segment do broadcast flows use?
cards.backHtml: Dynamic segments — membership is determined after the flow starts.

cards.front: What category of DMO can be used for engagement signals?
cards.back: Only DMOs categorized as Engagement.
cards.frontHtml: What category of DMO can be used for engagement signals?
cards.backHtml: Only DMOs categorized as Engagement.

cards.front: What are the four identifier types in an engagement signal?
cards.back: User Identifier, Timestamp Identifier, Item Identifier, Event Identifier.
cards.frontHtml: What are the four identifier types in an engagement signal?
cards.backHtml: User Identifier, Timestamp Identifier, Item Identifier, Event Identifier.

cards.front: What happens to flow sharing when a campaign is deleted?
cards.back: Sharing reverts to the flow's own rules; if none, the flow becomes private (owner, admins, View All Non-Setup Flows/Manage Flow only).
cards.frontHtml: What happens to flow sharing when a campaign is deleted?
cards.backHtml: Sharing reverts to the flow's own rules; if none, the flow becomes private (owner, admins, View All Non-Setup Flows/Manage Flow only).

cards.front: What's the REST endpoint to run an autolaunched flow?
cards.back: POST /services/data/v65.0/actions/custom/flow/FLOW API NAME
cards.frontHtml: What's the REST endpoint to run an autolaunched flow?
cards.backHtml: POST /services/data/v65.0/actions/custom/flow/FLOW_API_NAME

cards.front: What's the difference between Invocable.Action and Flow.Interview in Apex?
cards.back: Invocable.Action = dynamic reference + bulkification; Flow.Interview = static reference (referential integrity) but no bulkification.
cards.frontHtml: What's the difference between Invocable.Action and Flow.Interview in Apex?
cards.backHtml: Invocable.Action = dynamic reference + bulkification; Flow.Interview = static reference (referential integrity) but no bulkification.

cards.front: Which flow version does REST run vs. Apex-as-admin?
cards.back: REST runs the active version; Apex as flow admin runs the latest version regardless of activation.
cards.frontHtml: Which flow version does REST run vs. Apex-as-admin?
cards.backHtml: REST runs the active version; Apex as flow admin runs the latest version regardless of activation.

cards.front: What's the limit of associated journeys per Campaign?
cards.back: 20 journeys per Campaign.
cards.frontHtml: What's the limit of associated journeys per Campaign?
cards.backHtml: 20 journeys per Campaign.

cards.front: What journey modes are required to connect to a Campaign?
cards.back: Draft, Running, Finishing, Paused, or Stopped.
cards.frontHtml: What journey modes are required to connect to a Campaign?
cards.backHtml: Draft, Running, Finishing, Paused, or Stopped.

cards.front: Which flows don't appear on the Marketing Calendar?
cards.back: Event/form-triggered flows (no start date).
cards.frontHtml: Which flows don't appear on the Marketing Calendar?
cards.backHtml: Event/form-triggered flows (no start date).

decks.title: Flashcards — Marketing Cloud Next Setup & Data Foundation

cards.front: What three admin roles are involved in Marketing Cloud Next setup?
cards.back: Salesforce admin (System Administrator profile), Data Cloud admin (installs data kits, deploys streams, configures identity resolution & scoring), and Marketing admin (Marketing Cloud Admin permission set).
cards.frontHtml: What three admin roles are involved in Marketing Cloud Next setup?
cards.backHtml: Salesforce admin (System Administrator profile), Data Cloud admin (installs data kits, deploys streams, configures identity resolution & scoring), and Marketing admin (Marketing Cloud Admin permission set).

cards.front: What makes Marketing Cloud Next fundamentally different from legacy email tools?
cards.back: It's built natively on Data Cloud , so data unification, identity, segments, and AI all depend on the Data Cloud foundation.
cards.frontHtml: What makes Marketing Cloud Next fundamentally different from legacy email tools?
cards.backHtml: It's built natively on Data Cloud, so data unification, identity, segments, and AI all depend on the Data Cloud foundation.

cards.front: What two things must be enabled before accessing required/additional setup settings?
cards.back: Enable Data Cloud and enable Marketing Cloud Next in Basic Settings.
cards.frontHtml: What two things must be enabled before accessing required/additional setup settings?
cards.backHtml: Enable Data Cloud and enable Marketing Cloud Next in Basic Settings.

cards.front: What is a data kit, and what does installing one trigger?
cards.back: A pre-built package of DMOs, fields, and data connections. Installing auto-deploys its related data streams in Data Cloud.
cards.frontHtml: What is a data kit, and what does installing one trigger?
cards.backHtml: A pre-built package of DMOs, fields, and data connections. Installing auto-deploys its related data streams in Data Cloud.

cards.front: Which data kits are always required regardless of channel add-ons?
cards.back: Marketing Setup Objects, Consent Objects, Flows Integration, Email Channel, and Sales (accounts/leads/contacts). SMS/WhatsApp kits only for those add-ons.
cards.frontHtml: Which data kits are always required regardless of channel add-ons?
cards.backHtml: Marketing Setup Objects, Consent Objects, Flows Integration, Email Channel, and Sales (accounts/leads/contacts). SMS/WhatsApp kits only for those add-ons.

cards.front: What does an identity resolution ruleset do?
cards.back: Defines relationships among DMOs/fields so Data Cloud unifies related/duplicate records into Unified Individual records for targeting.
cards.frontHtml: What does an identity resolution ruleset do?
cards.backHtml: Defines relationships among DMOs/fields so Data Cloud unifies related/duplicate records into Unified Individual records for targeting.

cards.front: What three match rules are in a generated Individual ruleset?
cards.back: Normalized Email, Lead to Contact, and Device to Known.
cards.frontHtml: What three match rules are in a generated Individual ruleset?
cards.backHtml: Normalized Email, Lead to Contact, and Device to Known.

cards.front: Why does Salesforce recommend one ruleset per object?
cards.back: Identity resolution consumes Data Cloud credits; two active rulesets per object doubles billing.
cards.frontHtml: Why does Salesforce recommend one ruleset per object?
cards.backHtml: Identity resolution consumes Data Cloud credits; two active rulesets per object doubles billing.

cards.front: What's the key difference between Marketing Cloud Admin and Marketing Cloud Manager?
cards.back: Admin gets Salesforce Setup access; Manager gets full control on campaigns/segments/flows but no full Setup access.
cards.frontHtml: What's the key difference between Marketing Cloud Admin and Marketing Cloud Manager?
cards.backHtml: Admin gets Salesforce Setup access; Manager gets full control on campaigns/segments/flows but no full Setup access.

cards.front: Which CMS content role can manage users and sharing?
cards.back: Content Admin (also creates/publishes all content and assigns default brand).
cards.frontHtml: Which CMS content role can manage users and sharing?
cards.backHtml: Content Admin (also creates/publishes all content and assigns default brand).

cards.front: What two permission sets must an Identity-licensed marketing user receive?
cards.back: Marketing Cloud Manager + Tableau Next Included App Business User.
cards.frontHtml: What two permission sets must an Identity-licensed marketing user receive?
cards.backHtml: Marketing Cloud Manager + Tableau Next Included App Business User.

cards.front: What three things are required to send email?
cards.back: Authenticate a sending domain, verify a From address, and provide a physical address.
cards.frontHtml: What three things are required to send email?
cards.backHtml: Authenticate a sending domain, verify a From address, and provide a physical address.

cards.front: What do DKIM, SPF, and DMARC each do?
cards.back: DKIM adds a digital signature; SPF verifies the sending server is authorized; DMARC tells receivers how to handle failures.
cards.frontHtml: What do DKIM, SPF, and DMARC each do?
cards.backHtml: DKIM adds a digital signature; SPF verifies the sending server is authorized; DMARC tells receivers how to handle failures.

cards.front: What triggers auto-unsubscribe in Reply Mail Management?
cards.back: A manual reply containing unsub/unsubscribe/opt-out/remove/stop in the first 200 characters.
cards.frontHtml: What triggers auto-unsubscribe in Reply Mail Management?
cards.backHtml: A manual reply containing unsub/unsubscribe/opt-out/remove/stop in the first 200 characters.

cards.front: What three requests are needed for a 10-digit US long code?
cards.back: Brand Request, Campaign Request, and Code Request.
cards.frontHtml: What three requests are needed for a 10-digit US long code?
cards.backHtml: Brand Request, Campaign Request, and Code Request.

cards.front: Which channels are NOT supported in Government Cloud?
cards.back: SMS, WhatsApp, and Mobile App Messaging.
cards.frontHtml: Which channels are NOT supported in Government Cloud?
cards.backHtml: SMS, WhatsApp, and Mobile App Messaging.

cards.front: What does a single consent import correspond to, and what can't it do?
cards.back: One channel + one subscription + one status. It can't create new leads/contacts — only updates existing contact points.
cards.frontHtml: What does a single consent import correspond to, and what can't it do?
cards.backHtml: One channel + one subscription + one status. It can't create new leads/contacts — only updates existing contact points.

cards.front: What phone format is required for SMS/WhatsApp consent imports?
cards.back: ITU E.164 with country code, e.g. +12065550123.
cards.frontHtml: What phone format is required for SMS/WhatsApp consent imports?
cards.backHtml: ITU E.164 with country code, e.g. +12065550123.

cards.front: What four activities does web tracking track?
cards.back: Page views, form submissions, link clicks, button clicks.
cards.frontHtml: What four activities does web tracking track?
cards.backHtml: Page views, form submissions, link clicks, button clicks.

cards.front: What cookie stores the tracking consent decision?
cards.back: sfmc consent (True = opted in, False = opted out/ignored).
cards.frontHtml: What cookie stores the tracking consent decision?
cards.backHtml: sfmc_consent (True = opted in, False = opted out/ignored).

cards.front: What are the three score types?
cards.back: Engagement Score, Fit Score, and Overall Marketing Score (normalized 0–100).
cards.frontHtml: What are the three score types?
cards.backHtml: Engagement Score, Fit Score, and Overall Marketing Score (normalized 0–100).

cards.front: How must attribute values be entered in scoring rules?
cards.back: Exact, case-sensitive — e.g. "UNSUBSCRIBE" not "unsubscribe".
cards.frontHtml: How must attribute values be entered in scoring rules?
cards.backHtml: Exact, case-sensitive — e.g. "UNSUBSCRIBE" not "unsubscribe".

cards.front: Which edition supports account scoring?
cards.back: Advanced edition only.
cards.frontHtml: Which edition supports account scoring?
cards.backHtml: Advanced edition only.

cards.front: Which three Einstein features are Advanced edition only?
cards.back: Engagement Scoring, Engagement Frequency, and (partially) Send Time Optimization global model opt-out.
cards.frontHtml: Which three Einstein features are Advanced edition only?
cards.backHtml: Engagement Scoring, Engagement Frequency, and (partially) Send Time Optimization global model opt-out.

cards.front: Does a low or high Metrics Guard score indicate a real click?
cards.back: Low score = higher confidence it's real (high = machine-generated).
cards.frontHtml: Does a low or high Metrics Guard score indicate a real click?
cards.backHtml: Low score = higher confidence it's real (high = machine-generated).

cards.front: Which objects deploy first from sandbox to production?
cards.back: Data Cloud objects first (segments, DMOs, data graphs, calculated insights), then Marketing Cloud Next objects.
cards.frontHtml: Which objects deploy first from sandbox to production?
cards.backHtml: Data Cloud objects first (segments, DMOs, data graphs, calculated insights), then Marketing Cloud Next objects.

cards.front: What does the sandbox email blackhole do?
cards.back: Prevents test emails reaching real customer addresses (with up to 5 allowed domains); doesn't suppress Preview/Test or Debug flow sends.
cards.frontHtml: What does the sandbox email blackhole do?
cards.backHtml: Prevents test emails reaching real customer addresses (with up to 5 allowed domains); doesn't suppress Preview/Test or Debug flow sends.

cards.front: How many active flows do Growth vs. Advanced allow?
cards.back: Growth 500, Advanced 750.
cards.frontHtml: How many active flows do Growth vs. Advanced allow?
cards.backHtml: Growth 500, Advanced 750.

cards.front: What's the difference between contact point selection and source priority order ?
cards.back: Selection = which objects/fields (email, phone, MAID…) are included in an activation; source priority = which value wins when a contact has that data from multiple sources.
cards.frontHtml: What's the difference between contact point selection and source priority order?
cards.backHtml: Selection = which objects/fields (email, phone, MAID…) are included in an activation; source priority = which value wins when a contact has that data from multiple sources.

cards.front: Why can't reconciliation rules determine which contact point to deliver?
cards.back: Reconciliation rules only reconcile Unified Individual object fields — NOT unified contact point objects. Source priority controls contact-point delivery.
cards.frontHtml: Why can't reconciliation rules determine which contact point to deliver?
cards.backHtml: Reconciliation rules only reconcile Unified Individual object fields — NOT unified contact point objects. Source priority controls contact-point delivery.

cards.front: What do "Primary", "Personal", and "Business" priority values depend on?
cards.back: Primary = Primary Flag mapped in Data Streams; Personal = For Personal Use field = 1; Business = For Business Use field = 1 (Any = no Primary Flag mapped).
cards.frontHtml: What do "Primary", "Personal", and "Business" priority values depend on?
cards.backHtml: Primary = Primary Flag mapped in Data Streams; Personal = For Personal Use field = 1; Business = For Business Use field = 1 (Any = no Primary Flag mapped).

cards.front: What happens when you remove "Any Source/Any Type" from source priority?
cards.back: The activation uses only specific sources, so the population count drops (fewer sources = fewer matches).
cards.frontHtml: What happens when you remove "Any Source/Any Type" from source priority?
cards.backHtml: The activation uses only specific sources, so the population count drops (fewer sources = fewer matches).

cards.front: Which platforms have a fixed (unchangeable) default source priority order?
cards.back: B2C Commerce Cloud and MobilePush (MC Engagement → Primary).
cards.frontHtml: Which platforms have a fixed (unchangeable) default source priority order?
cards.backHtml: B2C Commerce Cloud and MobilePush (MC Engagement → Primary).

cards.front: Which activation targets accept the Email Address contact point?
cards.back: Cloud File Storage, External Platform, Marketing Cloud Personalization, and Marketing Cloud Engagement.
cards.frontHtml: Which activation targets accept the Email Address contact point?
cards.backHtml: Cloud File Storage, External Platform, Marketing Cloud Personalization, and Marketing Cloud Engagement.

cards.front: What are the three functional subdomains and their inbound purpose?
cards.back: reply (reply handling), bounce (bounce notifications), leave (unsubscribe requests) — each needs a CNAME to …inbound.[tenant].mx.salesforce.com .
cards.frontHtml: What are the three functional subdomains and their inbound purpose?
cards.backHtml: reply (reply handling), bounce (bounce notifications), leave (unsubscribe requests) — each needs a CNAME to …inbound.[tenant].mx.salesforce.com.

cards.front: Why is applying p=reject DMARC at the root domain risky?
cards.back: It affects ALL corporate email from that domain; misconfiguration can fail legitimate mail — coordinate with IT.
cards.frontHtml: Why is applying p=reject DMARC at the root domain risky?
cards.backHtml: It affects ALL corporate email from that domain; misconfiguration can fail legitimate mail — coordinate with IT.

cards.front: How does Marketing Cloud Next handle shared vs. dedicated IPs?
cards.back: Starts on shared IPs; automatically assigns dedicated IPs based on volume; continuously rebalances traffic across pools based on volume and delivery trends (managed — no manual IP management).
cards.frontHtml: How does Marketing Cloud Next handle shared vs. dedicated IPs?
cards.backHtml: Starts on shared IPs; automatically assigns dedicated IPs based on volume; continuously rebalances traffic across pools based on volume and delivery trends (managed — no manual IP management).

cards.front: Why must you warm your domain even though IPs are managed automatically?
cards.back: Major mailbox providers now use domain reputation as the PRIMARY sender-reputation signal (IP reputation is a fallback for unknown domains).
cards.frontHtml: Why must you warm your domain even though IPs are managed automatically?
cards.backHtml: Major mailbox providers now use domain reputation as the PRIMARY sender-reputation signal (IP reputation is a fallback for unknown domains).

cards.front: What's the recommended starting volume for a brand-new sending domain?
cards.back: No more than a few hundred emails per day, using a slow, methodical approach.
cards.frontHtml: What's the recommended starting volume for a brand-new sending domain?
cards.backHtml: No more than a few hundred emails per day, using a slow, methodical approach.

cards.front: What's the daily max volume on days 1–3 of the warming schedule?
cards.back: 500 emails (then 1,000 on days 4–5, 1,500 day 6, 2,000 day 7, 2,500 day 8).
cards.frontHtml: What's the daily max volume on days 1–3 of the warming schedule?
cards.backHtml: 500 emails (then 1,000 on days 4–5, 1,500 day 6, 2,000 day 7, 2,500 day 8).

cards.front: What are the bounce-rate and complaint-rate targets?
cards.back: Bounce rate < 2%; complaint rate < 0.1%.
cards.frontHtml: What are the bounce-rate and complaint-rate targets?
cards.backHtml: Bounce rate < 2%; complaint rate < 0.1%.

cards.front: What are the two spam-trap types and what does each signal?
cards.back: Honeypot (created to catch spammers → opt-in/purchased-data issues) vs. Recycled (reused after 6–12 months inactivity → list hygiene issues).
cards.frontHtml: What are the two spam-trap types and what does each signal?
cards.backHtml: Honeypot (created to catch spammers → opt-in/purchased-data issues) vs. Recycled (reused after 6–12 months inactivity → list hygiene issues).

cards.front: What three things does one-click List-Unsubscribe require?
cards.back: List-Unsubscribe + List-Unsubscribe-Post headers, HTTPS, and a DKIM signature.
cards.frontHtml: What three things does one-click List-Unsubscribe require?
cards.backHtml: List-Unsubscribe + List-Unsubscribe-Post headers, HTTPS, and a DKIM signature.

cards.front: What DKIM key size does Marketing Cloud Next use by default, and which records carry it?
cards.back: 2048-bit keys, carried by the 3 outbound CNAME records (s1/s2/s3-e360).
cards.frontHtml: What DKIM key size does Marketing Cloud Next use by default, and which records carry it?
cards.backHtml: 2048-bit keys, carried by the 3 outbound CNAME records (s1/s2/s3-e360).

cards.back: No — recommended but not required to activate; however, it IS required for bulk senders (Gmail/Yahoo). Related - marketing-cloud-next-overview - data-kits-and-data-streams - identity-resolution-rulesets - scoring-models - ai-features - sandbox-and-deployment

decks.title: Flashcards — Personalization Data Sources, Merge Fields, Dynamic Content & Repeaters

cards.front: What is a data source in Marketing Cloud Next, and where do you manage them?
cards.back: An object or element from your org that contains fields and data; its attributes become available for merge fields, expressions, repeaters, and dynamic content. Managed in the Data Sources tab of Content Builder.
cards.frontHtml: What is a data source in Marketing Cloud Next, and where do you manage them?
cards.backHtml: An object or element from your org that contains fields and data; its attributes become available for merge fields, expressions, repeaters, and dynamic content. Managed in the Data Sources tab of Content Builder.

cards.front: What must you do if you change a data source after its attributes are used in merge fields?
cards.back: Delete those merge fields, add the new data source, then recreate the merge fields.
cards.frontHtml: What must you do if you change a data source after its attributes are used in merge fields?
cards.backHtml: Delete those merge fields, add the new data source, then recreate the merge fields.

cards.front: What is a data graph, and what's it usually based on for personalization?
cards.back: A Data 360 object built from a primary DMO plus related objects, flattened into a streamlined table. For personalization it's usually a profile data graph based on the Unified Individual DMO.
cards.frontHtml: What is a data graph, and what's it usually based on for personalization?
cards.backHtml: A Data 360 object built from a primary DMO plus related objects, flattened into a streamlined table. For personalization it's usually a profile data graph based on the Unified Individual DMO.

cards.front: What's the trade-off between standard and real-time data graphs?
cards.back: Real-time graphs provide faster response times but cost more.
cards.frontHtml: What's the trade-off between standard and real-time data graphs?
cards.backHtml: Real-time graphs provide faster response times but cost more.

cards.front: When can't you remove or replace a data graph?
cards.back: If an email has dynamic content variations or a Personalization recommender; or when a landing page content block is published. For landing pages, use a real-time graph for better performance.
cards.frontHtml: When can't you remove or replace a data graph?
cards.backHtml: If an email has dynamic content variations or a Personalization recommender; or when a landing page content block is published. For landing pages, use a real-time graph for better performance.

cards.front: How do SMS and WhatsApp messages use the data graph?
cards.back: Only the default data graph is available; it doesn't appear in the Data Sources panel, but its data still works in merge fields.
cards.frontHtml: How do SMS and WhatsApp messages use the data graph?
cards.backHtml: Only the default data graph is available; it doesn't appear in the Data Sources panel, but its data still works in merge fields.

cards.front: What happens if you delete the default data graph, and what's the only personalization option in Starter/Pro Suite emails?
cards.back: The Unified Individual DMO data provider is the fallback. In Starter and Pro Suite emails, merge fields can only refer to the Unified Individual DMO.
cards.frontHtml: What happens if you delete the default data graph, and what's the only personalization option in Starter/Pro Suite emails?
cards.backHtml: The Unified Individual DMO data provider is the fallback. In Starter and Pro Suite emails, merge fields can only refer to the Unified Individual DMO.

cards.front: What are the limits of an Event data source?
cards.back: Max 1 event data source per content item; repeaters don't support custom event data in emails; once published you can't remove or replace it.
cards.frontHtml: What are the limits of an Event data source?
cards.backHtml: Max 1 event data source per content item; repeaters don't support custom event data in emails; once published you can't remove or replace it.

cards.front: What does an Offer data source do, and what's its limit?
cards.back: Delivers tailored promotions in email (name, description, coupon code) with dynamic content rules by attribute (e.g., loyalty tier). Max 5 offer data providers per email.
cards.frontHtml: What does an Offer data source do, and what's its limit?
cards.backHtml: Delivers tailored promotions in email (name, description, coupon code) with dynamic content rules by attribute (e.g., loyalty tier). Max 5 offer data providers per email.

cards.front: What rules govern Personalization Recommender data sources?
cards.back: Only trained recommenders based on the same data graph as the email are selectable; needs a training period with at least one successful refresh; you can replace but not remove them; data works only in a repeater and its merge fields.
cards.frontHtml: What rules govern Personalization Recommender data sources?
cards.backHtml: Only trained recommenders based on the same data graph as the email are selectable; needs a training period with at least one successful refresh; you can replace but not remove them; data works only in a repeater and its merge fields.

cards.front: What data types do content variables support?
cards.back: Boolean, string, date, date time, number, and recordId (references a Salesforce record). Mapped to any Flow data source including MuleSoft and HTTP connectors.
cards.frontHtml: What data types do content variables support?
cards.backHtml: Boolean, string, date, date time, number, and recordId (references a Salesforce record). Mapped to any Flow data source including MuleSoft and HTTP connectors.

cards.front: What are the rules for Lookup Data Graph data sources?
cards.back: Uses non-profile Data 360 data (e.g., product catalog) to complement the default graph; requires a primary key; can't be nested under other lookup providers; max 5 per content item.
cards.frontHtml: What are the rules for Lookup Data Graph data sources?
cards.backHtml: Uses non-profile Data 360 data (e.g., product catalog) to complement the default graph; requires a primary key; can't be nested under other lookup providers; max 5 per content item.

cards.front: What can an Apex Class data source do, and what's its limit?
cards.back: Passes data from a flow directly into content — simple parameters or complex structured data (order collections). One Apex class data source per message.
cards.frontHtml: What can an Apex Class data source do, and what's its limit?
cards.backHtml: Passes data from a flow directly into content — simple parameters or complex structured data (order collections). One Apex class data source per message.

cards.front: What does the Activation data source do, and what's its limit?
cards.back: References a Data 360 segmentation activation, making segment attributes available in email merge fields for real-time audience targeting. One activation data source per message.
cards.frontHtml: What does the Activation data source do, and what's its limit?
cards.backHtml: References a Data 360 segmentation activation, making segment attributes available in email merge fields for real-time audience targeting. One activation data source per message.

cards.front: Which data sources are available only on landing pages and forms?
cards.back: Marketing Object and Prospect (both via the read data provider).
cards.frontHtml: Which data sources are available only on landing pages and forms?
cards.backHtml: Marketing Object and Prospect (both via the read data provider).

cards.front: Where can you add merge fields in an email?
cards.back: In the subject line and preheader (Add Merge Field), or in the text of content via the Add Merge Field icon in the editing toolbar.
cards.frontHtml: Where can you add merge fields in an email?
cards.backHtml: In the subject line and preheader (Add Merge Field), or in the text of content via the Add Merge Field icon in the editing toolbar.

cards.front: What is a saved expression, and where is it stored?
cards.back: Saved filter and sort criteria across related data objects that select the right attribute for a merge field. Stored in Salesforce CMS; reusable in email, SMS, and WhatsApp.
cards.frontHtml: What is a saved expression, and where is it stored?

cards.front: What permissions are needed to create vs. publish an expression?
cards.back: Create/edit: Marketing Cloud Manager permission set + any CMS workspace contributor role. Publish/unpublish: Marketing Cloud Manager + a CMS workspace contributor role of content admin or content manager.
cards.frontHtml: What permissions are needed to create vs. publish an expression?

cards.front: What must be set up before you can create an expression?
cards.back: A data graph.
cards.frontHtml: What must be set up before you can create an expression?
cards.backHtml: A data graph.

cards.front: What is a personalization point?
cards.back: A content element eligible for a personalization decision (subject line, preheader, image component). Configuring the first variation auto-creates one for that component/field.
cards.frontHtml: What is a personalization point?
cards.backHtml: A content element eligible for a personalization decision (subject line, preheader, image component). Configuring the first variation auto-creates one for that component/field.

cards.front: What's the difference between a personalization decision and a targeting rule?
cards.back: A decision determines who's eligible for a response based on targeting rules (each variation relates to a decision with the same name). A targeting rule defines the conditions for showing a specific variation.
cards.frontHtml: What's the difference between a personalization decision and a targeting rule?
cards.backHtml: A decision determines who's eligible for a response based on targeting rules (each variation relates to a decision with the same name). A targeting rule defines the conditions for showing a specific variation.

cards.front: What are the limits for personalization points and variations?
cards.back: 25 personalization points per email/landing page; 15 variations per component. Subject line + preheader count as one component.
cards.frontHtml: What are the limits for personalization points and variations?
cards.backHtml: 25 personalization points per email/landing page; 15 variations per component. Subject line + preheader count as one component.

cards.front: What's the difference between "All Conditions Are Met" and "Any Conditions Are Met"?
cards.back: All = recipient must meet every condition; Any = recipient meets at least one condition.
cards.frontHtml: What's the difference between "All Conditions Are Met" and "Any Conditions Are Met"?
cards.backHtml: All = recipient must meet every condition; Any = recipient meets at least one condition.

cards.front: Can you change the priority of the default variation?
cards.back: No — the default variation's priority can't be changed; it shows when a recipient doesn't qualify for any personalized variation.
cards.frontHtml: Can you change the priority of the default variation?
cards.backHtml: No — the default variation's priority can't be changed; it shows when a recipient doesn't qualify for any personalized variation.

cards.front: What's the difference between cloning and linking a personalization point?
cards.back: Cloning creates a separate copy with its own rules/settings; linking shares one point so changes apply to all linked components. Linking requires the point to already exist in the content item and the component to have no variations.
cards.frontHtml: What's the difference between cloning and linking a personalization point?
cards.backHtml: Cloning creates a separate copy with its own rules/settings; linking shares one point so changes apply to all linked components. Linking requires the point to already exist in the content item and the component to have no variations.

cards.front: What happens when you add, delete, or edit a variation on a linked component?
cards.back: Adding a variation adds it to all linked components; deleting removes it everywhere; editing targeting rules or priorities applies to all linked components. Content and style edits stay independent.
cards.frontHtml: What happens when you add, delete, or edit a variation on a linked component?
cards.backHtml: Adding a variation adds it to all linked components; deleting removes it everywhere; editing targeting rules or priorities applies to all linked components. Content and style edits stay independent.

cards.front: What happens when you unlink a component from a personalization point?
cards.back: The personalization point is cloned (e.g., "Copy of Personalization Point A") so the component keeps its targeting rules, priorities, variations, content, and style, but becomes independent. Other components stay linked to the original.
cards.frontHtml: What happens when you unlink a component from a personalization point?
cards.backHtml: The personalization point is cloned (e.g., "Copy of Personalization Point A") so the component keeps its targeting rules, priorities, variations, content, and style, but becomes independent. Other components stay linked to the original.

cards.front: Can you export or import content that contains variations?
cards.back: No — content with variations can't be exported or imported.
cards.frontHtml: Can you export or import content that contains variations?
cards.backHtml: No — content with variations can't be exported or imported.

cards.front: What happens if a repeater source has no data for a recipient?
cards.back: The repeater appears empty when that recipient opens the email.
cards.frontHtml: What happens if a repeater source has no data for a recipient?
cards.backHtml: The repeater appears empty when that recipient opens the email.

cards.front: What happens if you change a repeater layout when it contains content or data?
cards.back: The content, data, and any style settings within the repeater get removed.
cards.frontHtml: What happens if you change a repeater layout when it contains content or data?
cards.backHtml: The content, data, and any style settings within the repeater get removed.

cards.front: What must you do if you change a repeater source after its attributes are used in merge fields?
cards.back: Delete those merge fields, add the new repeater source, then recreate the merge fields.
cards.frontHtml: What must you do if you change a repeater source after its attributes are used in merge fields?
cards.backHtml: Delete those merge fields, add the new repeater source, then recreate the merge fields.

cards.front: When adding a merge field inside a repeater, which item do you expand?
cards.back: The item with the same name as the repeater source — it's the first item in the Add Merge Field menu and contains the source's attributes.
cards.frontHtml: When adding a merge field inside a repeater, which item do you expand?

cards.front: Why must you allocate time when using a new recommender?
cards.back: The recommender needs a training period with at least one successful refresh before it can be used.
cards.frontHtml: Why must you allocate time when using a new recommender?

cards.front: How does an objective-based recommender differ from rule-based image variations?
cards.back: Instead of writing rules to decide which image each contact sees, the recommender chooses the best image for each contact at send time, learning from engagement over time.
cards.frontHtml: How does an objective-based recommender differ from rule-based image variations?

cards.front: Why does the design canvas show a placeholder for recommender content, and how do you see real output?
cards.back: The recommender chooses content per contact, so there's no single fixed result. Use Preview, enter parameters such as a segment to simulate a contact context, and review what the recommender returns.

decks.title: Flashcards — Landing Pages, Forms, External Forms & Marketing Sites

cards.front: Where are component/template landing pages vs. code-view landing pages hosted?
cards.back: Component/template pages → the auto-generated Marketing Landing Pages Experience Cloud site; code-view pages → a marketing site (managed from the Marketing Sites tab).
cards.frontHtml: Where are component/template landing pages vs. code-view landing pages hosted?
cards.backHtml: Component/template pages → the auto-generated Marketing Landing Pages Experience Cloud site; code-view pages → a marketing site (managed from the Marketing Sites tab).

cards.front: What permissions are needed to create vs. publish landing page content?
cards.back: Create/edit: Marketing Cloud Manager + any CMS workspace contributor role. Publish/unpublish: Marketing Cloud Manager + a CMS workspace contributor role of content admin or content manager. AMPscript authoring adds the AMPscript Author permission.
cards.frontHtml: What permissions are needed to create vs. publish landing page content?
cards.backHtml: Create/edit: Marketing Cloud Manager + any CMS workspace contributor role. Publish/unpublish: Marketing Cloud Manager + a CMS workspace contributor role of content admin or content manager. AMPscript authoring adds the AMPscript Author permission.

cards.front: When can you edit a landing page URL alias, and what happens on publish?
cards.back: Only in Draft status (default alias = title + content key). After publish you can't change it; publishing activates the alias.
cards.frontHtml: When can you edit a landing page URL alias, and what happens on publish?
cards.backHtml: Only in Draft status (default alias = title + content key). After publish you can't change it; publishing activates the alias.

cards.front: What happens when you publish a landing page that contains a form?
cards.back: The form is published and the flow related to the form is activated.
cards.frontHtml: What happens when you publish a landing page that contains a form?
cards.backHtml: The form is published and the flow related to the form is activated.

cards.front: What structured data format is allowed in landing page head tags?
cards.back: Only JSON-LD ( <script type="application/ld+json" ). Head tags don't support JavaScript; only <link , <meta , and <script tags are allowed.
cards.frontHtml: What structured data format is allowed in landing page head tags?
cards.backHtml: Only JSON-LD (<script type="application/ld+json">). Head tags don't support JavaScript; only <link>, <meta>, and <script> tags are allowed.

cards.front: What are the requirements for a landing page redirect URL?
cards.back: Must begin with https:// and be fewer than 2,000 characters. Set it up before unpublishing to avoid the "URL no longer exists" page.
cards.frontHtml: What are the requirements for a landing page redirect URL?
cards.backHtml: Must begin with https:// and be fewer than 2,000 characters. Set it up before unpublishing to avoid the "URL no longer exists" page.

cards.front: What's required to preview a landing page, and what's unresolved in preview?
cards.back: You must be a site contributor to the Marketing Landing Pages site. Merge fields are unresolved in preview; external images need their domain in the Trusted URL list.
cards.frontHtml: What's required to preview a landing page, and what's unresolved in preview?
cards.backHtml: You must be a site contributor to the Marketing Landing Pages site. Merge fields are unresolved in preview; external images need their domain in the Trusted URL list.

cards.front: What does locking a landing page template component protect — and what doesn't it protect?
cards.back: It protects content and settings only. Authors can still edit targeting rules, add/delete variations, and modify personalization logic on locked components — clone the personalization point for control over the logic.
cards.frontHtml: What does locking a landing page template component protect — and what doesn't it protect?

cards.front: What happens when a marketer creates a landing page from a template with dynamic content?
cards.back: All dynamic content rules and variants are copied to the new landing page automatically. The fallback variant renders when no rules match or the data lookup fails.
cards.frontHtml: What happens when a marketer creates a landing page from a template with dynamic content?
cards.backHtml: All dynamic content rules and variants are copied to the new landing page automatically. The fallback variant renders when no rules match or the data lookup fails.

cards.front: What one-time admin setup is needed for LinkedIn posts?
cards.back: Add the Social Posts related list to the campaigns object (Object Manager → Campaigns Layout → Related List), then connect a LinkedIn account via Manage Connections.
cards.frontHtml: What one-time admin setup is needed for LinkedIn posts?
cards.backHtml: Add the Social Posts related list to the campaigns object (Object Manager → Campaigns Layout → Related List), then connect a LinkedIn account via Manage Connections.

cards.front: What are the minimum requirements for a form, and the unique names for submission fields?
cards.back: At least one input component and one button. Email field = unique name Email, first name = FirstName, last name = LastName (case-insensitive, no extra characters/spaces).
cards.frontHtml: What are the minimum requirements for a form, and the unique names for submission fields?
cards.backHtml: At least one input component and one button. Email field = unique name Email, first name = FirstName, last name = LastName (case-insensitive, no extra characters/spaces).

cards.front: How many forms per landing page, and how many flows per form?
cards.back: One form per landing page; a form relates to only one flow. View modes must match (block ↔ block, code ↔ code).
cards.frontHtml: How many forms per landing page, and how many flows per form?
cards.backHtml: One form per landing page; a form relates to only one flow. View modes must match (block ↔ block, code ↔ code).

cards.front: What objects can a form's write data provider use, and what's the default?
cards.back: Account, Contact, Lead, Prospect, or an available marketing object. If a marketing object is available it's the default; otherwise the form defaults to Lead. Only one write data source object at a time.
cards.frontHtml: What objects can a form's write data provider use, and what's the default?
cards.backHtml: Account, Contact, Lead, Prospect, or an available marketing object. If a marketing object is available it's the default; otherwise the form defaults to Lead. Only one write data source object at a time.

cards.front: What can a form's read data providers supply, and what's the lookup limit?
cards.back: Pre-fill fields and drive progressive profiling (they don't receive submitted data). Sources: recipient data graph, marketing object, or Prospect; up to 2 lookup data providers (max 1 marketing object + 1 recipient data graph).
cards.frontHtml: What can a form's read data providers supply, and what's the lookup limit?

cards.front: Which field types are supported on forms, and which standard field isn't?
cards.back: Checkbox, Date, Date/Time, Time, Email, Phone Number, Number, Picklist, Text, Text Area, Text Area (Long), URL. Number of Employees (Account/Lead/Prospect) isn't supported.
cards.frontHtml: Which field types are supported on forms, and which standard field isn't?
cards.backHtml: Checkbox, Date, Date/Time, Time, Email, Phone Number, Number, Picklist, Text, Text Area, Text Area (Long), URL. Number of Employees (Account/Lead/Prospect) isn't supported.

cards.front: What happens if you edit a CRM field's API name after using it in a form?
cards.back: Any new data submitted to that field isn't saved. Also, a data source field can appear only once on a form (no duplicates).
cards.frontHtml: What happens if you edit a CRM field's API name after using it in a form?

cards.front: What's required for a hidden form field marked as required?
cards.back: A fallback value — used when the URL parameter is invalid or missing. Hidden fields are visible on the canvas but not in preview/live form.
cards.frontHtml: What's required for a hidden form field marked as required?

cards.front: Where does Google reCAPTCHA v2 apply, and what breaks it?
cards.back: Only marketing landing pages with forms (not LWR/template sites); once enabled it shows on every form. Changing My Domain breaks it on existing published sites — add the new domain in the Google admin console.

cards.front: What are the restrictions on progressive profiling rules?
cards.back: Can't add a rule to a hidden field; can't hide a field that has a profile rule; can't apply to a related object. Changing the read data provider/source removes all rule connections.
cards.frontHtml: What are the restrictions on progressive profiling rules?

cards.front: What should you avoid pre-filling in forms?
cards.back: Personally identifiable information such as Social Security numbers or credit card numbers.
cards.frontHtml: What should you avoid pre-filling in forms?

cards.front: What happens when you unpublish a form?
cards.back: Its flow is deactivated and the Submit button stops working (an in-flight submission still completes). The form reverts to draft; to edit/republish, save the flow as a new version.
cards.frontHtml: What happens when you unpublish a form?
